definition_zh: 鬼；幽灵；幽灵般的人；隐约的一点；替写他人作品的人（作动词）
definition_en: the spirit of a dead person that some people believe they can see, or something faint and vague like such a spirit
core_image: 夜里的白影：一缕看不见身体的人形浮在旧屋里
scene: 老房子的走廊尽头，孩子说看见一团白影一闪而过。The children said a ghost walked along the corridor of the old house.
sceneCN: 这里 ghost 是「鬼；幽灵」（第 1 个义项：死者的灵魂显现）；句意为孩子们说一个幽灵在老房子的走廊里走过。

derivatives.zh: 由 ghost 加 -ly 构成，义为「幽灵般的；可怕的」
由 ghost 加 -like 构成，义为「像鬼一样的」
由 ghost 加 -ing 构成，义为「忽然断联；淡出式失联」

senses.title: The spirit of a dead person
senses.definition: the spirit of a dead person that people believe appears to the living
senses.definitionCN: 人们相信会向活人显现的死者的灵魂
senses.example: She claimed she saw a ghost in the attic.
senses.exampleCN: 她说她在阁楼上看见了幽灵。
senses.why: The core image is a visible person-shape without a body, so the oldest sense is the departed soul that still walks.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是「有人的形状却没有身体」，所以最早的义项就是仍在走动的死者灵魂。

senses.title: A faint trace of something
senses.definition: a very small amount or weak trace of something, often following 'the ghost of'
senses.definitionCN: 某物极小的一点或微弱残迹，常用于「the ghost of」结构
senses.example: There was not the ghost of a chance of winning.
senses.exampleCN: 连一丝获胜的机会都没有。
senses.why: A ghost is barely there, so English extends it to anything so faint it is almost nothing.
senses.whyCN: 鬼影似有似无，英语便用它指微弱到几乎不存在的痕迹。

senses.title: A ghostwriter
senses.definition: a writer whose work is officially credited to another person
senses.definitionCN: 作品署名为他人、实际代写的作者
senses.example: He worked as a ghost for two famous politicians.
senses.exampleCN: 他曾为两位著名政治人物代笔。
senses.why: The written text appears under one name but the invisible hand of another shaped it, like a hidden spirit.
senses.whyCN: 文字署着一个人的名字，却由一只看不见的手写成，就像隐形的幽灵。

senses.title: To ghostwrite
senses.definition: to write a book or article for someone else who is named as the author
senses.definitionCN: 替署名作者撰写书籍或文章
senses.example: She ghosted three novels before publishing her own name.
senses.exampleCN: 她代写了三部小说之后才用自己的名字出版。
senses.why: The verb grows from the hidden-writer sense: the real author stays unseen like a spirit.
senses.whyCN: 动词从「隐形写手」义项生长而来：真正的作者像幽灵一样不被看见。

senses.title: A faint image or echo
senses.definition: a faint secondary image or an unwanted faint signal or echo
senses.definitionCN: 微弱的次级影像或多余的低弱信号、回声
senses.example: The old film print left ghost images on the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 老旧的电影胶片在银幕上留下了残影。
senses.why: A ghost image is a weak copy of something stronger, keeping the idea of a barely visible form.
senses.whyCN: 残像是强影像的微弱副本，保留了「似有似无的形状」这一意象。

intro.en: Ghost is one of the oldest words in English, running straight back to the Germanic spirit-word.
intro.cn: ghost 是英语里最古老的词之一，直接追溯到日耳曼语的「灵魂」一词。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic root gheustoz meant spirit or breath.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼词根 gheustoz 意为灵魂或气息。

items.en: Old English gast meant spirit, soul, breath, and also a frightening apparition.
items.cn: 古英语 gast 意为灵魂、气息，也指吓人的鬼怪显现。

items.en: Norse gaver and related forms reinforced the Germanic family in northern England.
items.cn: 诺斯语的 gaver 等相关形式加强了英格兰北部的这一日耳曼词族。

items.en: Middle English spelled it gost or goost; the h appeared later under Flemish influence.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 gost 或 goost；字母 h 后来受佛兰芒语影响才加入。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling ghost; Holy Ghost survives as a religious term for the Holy Spirit.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 ghost；Holy Ghost 作为圣灵的宗教用语留存至今。

note.en: The words below share ghost's sound or its spirit-family of meanings.
note.cn: 下面的词与 ghost 音近，或同属「灵魂、显现」的义场。

entries.definition: Ghost-like in appearance; pale and frightening.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「幽灵般的；惨白可怕的」，由 ghost 直接派生。

entries.definition: A person staying at your home; only one letter different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「客人」，拼写与 ghost 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: An evil spirit that robs graves in Arabic folklore; sounds close to ghost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「食尸鬼」，源于阿拉伯民间传说，读音接近 ghost。

entries.definition: The non-physical part of a person, or a supernatural being.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灵魂；神灵」，比 ghost 更宽泛，可指人的精神。

entries.definition: A ghost or something seen that is not real.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幻影；幽灵」，偏书面，也指虚幻之物。

entries.definition: A ghost, especially a frightening one; British spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鬼怪；萦绕心头的恐惧」，英式拼写，美式作 specter。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of ghost.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Old English gast meant breath as well as soul, since breathing is the sign of life.
normal.cn: 古英语 gast 既指灵魂也指气息，因为呼吸是生命的标志。

normal.en: The h in ghost arrived from Flemish typesetters, so the spelling is later than the sound.
normal.cn: ghost 的 h 来自佛兰芒排字工，拼写比读音晚出现。

normal.en: Holy Ghost still names the Holy Spirit in Christian texts.
normal.cn: 基督教文本仍用 Holy Ghost 指圣灵。

normal.en: A ghost writer is the invisible author behind a famous name.
normal.cn: ghost writer 是名人之名背后看不见的作者。

normal.en: Ghost town is a town whose people have all gone, leaving empty streets.
normal.cn: ghost town 指居民全部离开、街道空荡的废城。

abstract.en: Picture a white shape in a dark corridor: it has a person's outline but no face.
abstract.cn: 想象黑走廊里一团白影：有人的轮廓却没有脸。

abstract.en: Think of a cold spot in a warm room where something unseen stands.
abstract.cn: 想象温暖的房间里有一处冷点，那里站着看不见的东西。

abstract.en: See a thin echo of a smile that disappears when you look straight at it.
abstract.cn: 想象一抹若有若无的微笑，你直视它时它就消失。

examples.en: The children said a ghost walked along the corridor of the old house.
examples.cn: 孩子们说一个幽灵在老房子的走廊里走过。

examples.en: He worked as a ghost for two famous politicians.
examples.cn: 他曾为两位著名政治人物代笔。

examples.en: There was not the ghost of a chance of winning.
examples.cn: 连一丝获胜的机会都没有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「够死特」——鬼魂够吓人，死去的灵魂特别地出现；ghost 让人想起黑屋里的白影

root: ghost 源自日耳曼语词根 gheustoz（灵魂、气息），经古英语 gast 直传至今；与德语 Geist（精神）同源，词族纯属日耳曼，与拉丁 spiritus 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of ghost keeps the same picture: something present in shape but absent in body.
sensesIntro.cn: ghost 的每个义项都保留同一画面：有形无实的存在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person-shape with no body, faintly visible
core.cn: 核心意象：有人的轮廓却没有身体、隐约可见的存在

branches.cn: 微弱到几乎不存在的痕迹或回声
署名背后隐形的写作者

intro.en: Ghost is a Germanic base word, so its items are its own endings and the compounds it forms.
intro.cn: ghost 是日耳曼基础词，下面列出它自身的词尾和构成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin has spiritus for breath and soul; it is a parallel tradition, not the source of ghost.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语以 spiritus 表示气息与灵魂，是与日耳曼传统平行的体系，并非 ghost 的来源。

items.example: Old English gast covered both soul and monster.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 gast 兼指灵魂与怪影。

definition_zh: 礼物；赠品；天赋；赠送（作动词）
definition_en: something given freely to someone, or a natural ability; as a verb, to give something as a present
core_image: 双手捧着递出的盒子：不图回报地交到对方手里
scene: 生日会上，妹妹捧着一个缎带盒子走到姐姐面前。She gave her sister a gift wrapped with a red ribbon.
sceneCN: 这里 gift 是「礼物；赠品」（第 1 个义项：无偿送出的东西）；句意为她送给姐姐一份系着红丝带的礼物。

derivatives.zh: 由 gift 加 -ed 构成，义为「有天赋的」
由 gifted 加 -ness 构成，义为「天赋资质」
由 gift 加 -ing 构成，义为「送礼行为」

senses.title: A present given freely
senses.definition: something given to someone without payment, usually to show friendship or love
senses.definitionCN: 无偿送给别人的东西，通常表达友谊或爱意
senses.example: He brought a gift to the host's birthday party.
senses.exampleCN: 他为主人的生日聚会带了礼物。
senses.why: The core image is hands passing a box for nothing in return, so the everyday sense is the present itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是双手捧盒递出而不求回报，所以日常义项就是礼物本身。

senses.title: A natural ability or talent
senses.definition: a natural ability to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 天生就擅长做某事的能力
senses.example: She has a gift for making people laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 她有逗人发笑的天赋。
senses.why: A talent arrives as if handed to you at birth, like a present you never asked for.
senses.whyCN: 才能仿佛出生时就被交到你手上，像一份未曾索取的礼物。

senses.title: The act or right of giving
senses.definition: the act of giving, or the legal transfer of property without payment
senses.definitionCN: 赠送的行为，或无偿转移财产的法律行为
senses.example: The land came to the museum by gift.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地是无偿赠予博物馆的。
senses.why: Behind every present is the action of giving, so law borrows the word for free transfer.
senses.whyCN: 每份礼物背后都有赠送这一行为，法律便借该词指无偿转让。

senses.title: To give as a present
senses.definition: to give something to someone as a present, often formally
senses.definitionCN: （常指正式地）把某物作为礼物送给某人
senses.example: The company gifted new books to every pupil.
senses.exampleCN: 公司给每个学生赠送了新书。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb when the giving is the point: hands offer the box again.
senses.whyCN: 当赠送本身成为重点，名词就转为动词：双手再次递出盒子。

senses.title: A natural endowment
senses.definition: natural powers or abilities collectively, in phrases like free gift of nature
senses.definitionCN: 自然禀赋的集合，如「自然的无偿馈赠」
senses.example: Fresh air and sunlight are the free gifts of nature.
senses.exampleCN: 新鲜空气和阳光是大自然的无偿馈赠。
senses.why: What nature gives costs nothing, so large blessings are also called gifts.
senses.whyCN: 大自然所给予的分文不取，宏大的恩赐也因此被称为 gifts。

intro.en: Gift comes straight from the Germanic word for giving, so gift and give are twins.
intro.cn: gift 直接来自日耳曼语「给予」一词，因此 gift 与 give 是孪生词。

items.en: The Germanic root geb- meant to give, appearing in give, gift and Germanic kin words.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 geb- 意为给予，出现在 give、gift 及同族词中。

items.en: Old Norse gift meant both a giving and a marriage, reinforcing the northern form.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 gift 兼指给予与婚姻，强化了北方的词形。

items.en: Old English gift meant payment for a wife, that is, bride-price or marriage.
items.cn: 古英语 gift 指娶妻的聘礼，即彩礼或婚姻。

items.en: Middle English widened gift to any present given freely.
items.cn: 中古英语把 gift 扩展为任何无偿赠送之物。

items.en: Modern English added the talent sense and later the verb, following Danish givte.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了天赋义，后又仿丹麦语 givte 发展出动词。

note.en: These words stand close to gift in spelling or in the world of giving and talent.
note.cn: 以下词与 gift 拼写相近，或同属赠送与天赋的义场。

entries.definition: Having natural talent; directly built on gift.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有天赋的」，直接由 gift 派生。

entries.definition: A paid performance by a musician; one letter different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（乐手的）演出」，与 gift 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: An obsolete spelling once confused with gift.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上曾与 gift 混用的旧拼法，现已废弃。

entries.definition: A thing given to someone, especially on an occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「礼物」，与 gift 最常用互换，场合感更强。

entries.definition: A natural ability to do something well.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「才能」，对应 gift 的天赋义项。

entries.definition: Money or goods given to a charity or cause.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「捐赠」，多为公益语境的赠送。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of gift.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Gift and give share the same Germanic root geb-, to hand over.
normal.cn: gift 与 give 共享日耳曼词根 geb-，意为交出。

normal.en: Old Norse gift also meant marriage, since marriage was once a contract sealed by payment.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 gift 还指婚姻，因为婚姻曾是靠聘礼缔结的契约。

normal.en: A gifted child is one whose ability was given by nature.
normal.cn: gifted child 指天资是自然赋予的孩子。

normal.en: German still says das Gift for poison, an old meaning split that learners must not copy.
normal.cn: 德语 das Gift 意为毒药，是同词族的分化义，学习者不可照搬。

normal.en: A gift shop sells small presents near museums and parks.
normal.cn: gift shop 指博物馆、公园附近的礼品店。

abstract.en: Picture two open hands: one holds a small box, the other stays empty, expecting nothing.
abstract.cn: 想象两只摊开的手：一只托着小盒子，另一只空着、无所期待。

abstract.en: See a ribbon being untied slowly, the moment a present becomes someone's own.
abstract.cn: 想象丝带被缓缓解开，礼物从此属于对方的瞬间。

abstract.en: Think of a seed dropped into your palm before you were born, growing into a talent.
abstract.cn: 想象出生前落进你掌心的一粒种子，后来长成才能。

examples.en: She gave her sister a gift wrapped with a red ribbon.
examples.cn: 她送给姐姐一份系着红丝带的礼物。

examples.en: She has a gift for making people laugh.
examples.cn: 她有逗人发笑的天赋。

examples.en: The company gifted new books to every pupil.
examples.cn: 公司给每个学生赠送了新书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「给伏特」——把礼物给予对方，伏在桌上打开；gift 由 give 加名词化尾巴而来

root: gift 源自日耳曼词根 geb-（给），是 give 的名词化形式；古诺斯语 gift 兼指婚姻，德语同源词 Gift 已分化为「毒药」义。

sensesIntro.en: Gift moves from the handed-over box to the ability that is handed to us at birth.
sensesIntro.cn: gift 的义项从递出的盒子延伸到出生时就被赋予的才能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something passed from open hands with no return asked
core.cn: 核心意象：从摊开的手中递出、不求回报之物

intro.en: Gift is a Germanic base, so the items below are its endings and the compounds it builds.
intro.cn: gift 是日耳曼基础词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin donum means a gift; it is the parallel Latin family, not the source of gift.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 donum 意为礼物，属平行的拉丁词族，并非 gift 的来源。

items.example: Norse gift covered giving and marriage alike.
items.exampleCN: 古诺斯语 gift 兼指给予与婚姻。

definition_zh: 女孩；姑娘；女儿；女职员
definition_en: a female child or young woman, or a daughter; informally, a female worker
core_image: 扎着辫子的小姑娘：还没长成大人的女性
scene: 课间的操场上，一个小姑娘正和同伴跳绳。The girl skipped rope with her friends in the playground.
sceneCN: 这里 girl 是「女孩；小姑娘」（第 1 个义项：年幼的女性）；句意为那个女孩在操场上和朋友们跳绳。

derivatives.zh: 由 girl 加 -hood 构成，义为「少女时代」
由 girl 加 -ish 构成，义为「少女似的；孩子气的」
girl 与 friend 的复合词，义为「女朋友」

senses.title: A female child
senses.definition: a female child, usually one who is not yet grown up
senses.definitionCN: 尚未长大的女性儿童
senses.example: The girl skipped rope with her friends in the playground.
senses.exampleCN: 女孩在操场上和朋友们跳绳。
senses.why: The core image is a young female not yet adult, which is the plainest everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是尚未成年的女性，这是最直白的日常义项。

senses.title: A young unmarried woman
senses.definition: a young woman, especially one who is unmarried
senses.definitionCN: 年轻女子，尤指未婚者
senses.example: She was a lively girl of twenty when she joined the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她进公司时是个二十岁的活泼姑娘。
senses.why: Once the child grows up, the same word stretches to the young woman who is not yet married.
senses.whyCN: 孩子长大后，同一个词便延伸到尚未婚嫁的年轻女子。

senses.title: A daughter
senses.definition: one's female child
senses.definitionCN: 某人的女性子女
senses.example: Their girl is studying medicine at university.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的女儿在大学学医。
senses.why: Family speech treats the child at home as my girl, so daughter grows out of the family picture.
senses.whyCN: 家庭口语把家里的女孩称作 my girl，女儿义便由此生长。

senses.title: A female worker
senses.definition: a woman employed in an office or service, in older informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 旧式口语中在办公室或服务行业工作的女性
senses.example: The girls in the office stayed late to finish the report.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室的女职员们加班到很晚才完成报告。
senses.why: Workplaces once called every junior female employee a girl, keeping the young-person frame.
senses.whyCN: 旧时职场把所有基层女性雇员都称作 girl，延续了「年轻人」的框架。

senses.title: Women of one's own circle
senses.definition: women friends together, in the friendly phrase the girls
senses.definitionCN: 女性朋友们的总称，用于友好表达 the girls
senses.example: She spends Friday nights out with the girls.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周五晚上和姐妹们外出。
senses.why: When girls grow up together, the group keeps the childhood word as a warm nickname.
senses.whyCN: 一起长大的女性群体保留童年旧称，作为亲昵的称呼。

intro.en: Girl once meant a child of either sex; the female-only meaning came later.
intro.cn: girl 最初指不分性别的孩子，「只指女性」是后来的事。

items.en: Middle English girle meant a child or young person of either sex, about twelve to fourteen.
items.cn: 中古英语 girle 指男女不限的孩子或少年，约十二至十四岁。

items.en: The further source is uncertain; some link it to Old English gyrele, a young person of low rank.
items.cn: 更早来源不确定；一说与古英语 gyrele（地位低下的年轻人）有关。

items.en: Some scholars point to Old Norse gilla, meaning to scream, as a possible relative.
items.cn: 一说与古诺斯语 gilla（尖叫）有亲属关系的可能。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the word had narrowed to a female child.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，词义已缩小为女孩。

items.en: Modern English kept girl for a female child and extended it to young women, daughters and female staff.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「女孩」义，并延伸到年轻女子、女儿与女性职员。

note.en: The words below resemble girl in sound or sit near it in the family circle.
note.cn: 以下词与 girl 音近，或同属家庭与年轻女性义场。

entries.definition: The breathing organ of a fish; one letter different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鱼鳃」，与 girl 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: A twist of hair; rhymes with girl.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卷发；卷曲」，与 girl 押韵，词义无关。

entries.definition: The period of being a girl.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「少女时代」，由 girl 直接派生。

entries.definition: A male child; the male counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「男孩」，girl 的男性对应词。

entries.definition: A young unmarried woman, in older or literary use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「少女」，书面或旧式用法。

entries.definition: A girl or young woman, chiefly Scottish and northern English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「少女」，主要用于苏格兰及英格兰北部。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of girl.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Middle English girle meant any child; sex came into the word only in the fifteenth century.
normal.cn: 中古英语 girle 指任何孩子，性别含义十五世纪才出现。

normal.en: Girlfriend joins girl and friend and now usually means a romantic partner.
normal.cn: girlfriend 由 girl 与 friend 复合，今多指恋爱对象。

normal.en: Girlhood names the years between childhood and womanhood.
normal.cn: girlhood 指童年与成年女性之间的岁月。

normal.en: The girls as a friendly phrase means a woman's own circle of friends.
normal.cn: the girls 作友好说法指女性的朋友圈。

normal.en: Girlish describes behaviour that looks young and childlike.
normal.cn: girlish 形容显得年少孩子气的行为。

abstract.en: Picture skipping ropes and school uniforms: a small figure laughing on the playground.
abstract.cn: 想象跳绳与校服：操场上一个小小的身影在笑。

abstract.en: See two braids swinging as someone runs down the corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象奔跑时两条辫子在走廊里摆动。

abstract.en: Think of a grown woman who still hears her childhood nickname among old friends.
abstract.cn: 想象一位成年女性在老友间仍被喊着童年的昵称。

examples.en: The girl skipped rope with her friends in the playground.
examples.cn: 女孩在操场上和朋友们跳绳。

examples.en: Their girl is studying medicine at university.
examples.cn: 他们的女儿在大学学医。

examples.en: She spends Friday nights out with the girls.
examples.cn: 她每周五晚上和姐妹们外出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哥欧」——哥和哦之间站着一个扎辫子的女孩；girl 读起来像轻轻喊一声小丫头

root: girl 来源不确定，一般认为与中古英语 gyrele（低阶年轻人）有关；本为中性「孩子」，十五世纪起专指女孩。

sensesIntro.en: Girl starts as any child, narrows to the female child, and then stretches to daughter, young woman and colleague.
sensesIntro.cn: girl 起初泛指孩子，缩为女孩，再延伸到女儿、年轻女子与女职员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young female figure before adulthood
core.cn: 核心意象：尚未成年的年轻女性身影

intro.en: Girl is a simple base noun; the items below are its endings and compounds.
intro.cn: girl 是简单的名词基础词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin puella means girl; it is the Latin parallel, not the source of girl.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 puella 意为女孩，是平行的拉丁词，并非 girl 的来源。

items.meaning: a child; later a female child
items.example: Middle English girle meant a child of either sex.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语 girle 男女皆可指。

definition_zh: 给；给予；赠送；提供；引起；让步（作名词）
definition_en: to hand something to someone, offer it, cause a feeling, or bend slightly under pressure
core_image: 摊开的手掌把东西交到另一只手里
scene: 雨天放学，同桌把伞柄塞进你的手里。The classmate gave his umbrella to his friend at the school gate.
sceneCN: 这里 give 是「把某物交到对方手里」（第 1 个义项：交付；给予）；句意为同桌在校门口把伞给了朋友。

derivatives.zh: 由 give 加 -er 构成，义为「给予者」
give 的同根名词形式，义为「礼物」
由 give 加 -ing 构成，义为「给予；施予」

senses.title: To hand something over
senses.definition: to put something into someone's hands or offer it to them
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到对方手里或递给对方
senses.example: The classmate gave his umbrella to his friend at the school gate.
senses.exampleCN: 同桌在校门口把伞给了朋友。
senses.why: The core image is an open hand passing an object forward, the plainest act of transfer.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是摊开的手把物件向前递出，是最直白的转移动作。

senses.title: To cause a feeling or state
senses.definition: to cause someone to have a feeling, problem, or chance
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生某种感觉、问题或机会
senses.example: The long climb gave him a dizzy feeling.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间的攀登使他感到眩晕。
senses.why: What is handed over need not be a thing: a feeling or chance can be placed in someone too.
senses.whyCN: 被递出的不必是实物：感觉与机会同样可以被放到对方身上。

senses.title: To perform or provide
senses.definition: to perform an action such as a speech, or provide help or information
senses.definitionCN: 发表演讲等行为，或提供帮助、信息
senses.example: The head teacher gave a speech at the opening ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在开学典礼上发表了演讲。
senses.why: A speech or help is not an object, yet it passes from speaker to audience like a gift.
senses.whyCN: 演讲与帮助虽非实物，却像礼物一样从一方传到另一方。

senses.title: To bend under pressure
senses.definition: to move or bend slightly when pressed, or to stop resisting
senses.definitionCN: 受压时轻微移动弯曲，或停止抵抗
senses.example: The wooden bridge gives a little when trucks cross.
senses.exampleCN: 木桥在卡车驶过时会轻微下弯。
senses.why: A hand that holds firmly can still loosen a little; materials yield the same way.
senses.whyCN: 握紧的手也会稍微松开；材料同样如此退让。

senses.title: To stop holding or doing
senses.definition: to stop trying or to surrender something, in give up
senses.definitionCN: 在 give up 中表示停止尝试或交出
senses.example: She gave up sugary drinks for a whole year.
senses.exampleCN: 她整整一年没喝含糖饮料。
senses.why: The hand that was holding something opens and lets go, ending the holding.
senses.whyCN: 握着的手摊开松开，持有就此结束。

intro.en: Give is a core Germanic verb, and its noun gift was born from it.
intro.cn: give 是日耳曼语的核心动词，名词 gift 就诞生于它。

items.en: The reconstructed root gebhan meant to give, shared across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构词根 gebhan 意为给予，遍布日耳曼各语言。

items.en: Old Norse gefa shaped the northern form of the verb in England.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 gefa 塑造了英格兰北部该动词的形式。

items.en: Old English giefan meant to give; past tense geaf, participle giefen.
items.cn: 古英语 giefan 意为给予，过去式 geaf，分词 giefen。

items.en: Middle English evened the forms into geven with the modern vowel.
items.cn: 中古英语把词形整化为 geven，元音趋于现代。

items.en: Modern English fixed give, gave, given and extended senses to yielding and causing.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 give、gave、given，并延伸出让步与引起义。

note.en: The words below echo give in sound or live in the same field of handing things over.
note.cn: 以下词与 give 音近，或同属「交付、给予」义场。

entries.definition: To be alive or reside; only the first sound differs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居住；活着」，与 give 仅首音不同。

entries.definition: The person who gives something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「给予者」，由 give 直接派生。

entries.definition: To stop being angry at a fault; built on give.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「原谅」，由 for- 加 give 构成，同根。

entries.definition: To present something for someone to accept or refuse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提出；提供」，强调对方的接受与否尚待决定。

entries.definition: To give money or goods to a good cause.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「捐赠」，多用于公益语境。

entries.definition: To give something formally, as a right or request.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「准予；授予」，偏正式。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of give.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Give, gave, given is one of English's oldest irregular patterns.
normal.cn: give、gave、given 是英语最古老的不规则变化之一。

normal.en: Forgive and forgive-and-forget keep give inside an older verb family.
normal.cn: forgive 等词让 give 保留在古老的动词家族里。

normal.en: Give in means the hand loosens and resistance ends.
normal.cn: give in 指手松开、抵抗结束。

normal.en: Give off is used for heat, light and smells leaving an object.
normal.cn: give off 用于热量、光和气味从物体散发。

normal.en: The noun give describes how much a seat or rope bends.
normal.cn: 名词 give 描述座椅或绳索的弹性程度。

abstract.en: Picture an open palm tilting forward until the object slides into another hand.
abstract.cn: 想象摊开的掌心向前倾，物件滑入另一只手。

abstract.en: See an umbrella handle pushed gently into your grip in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨天里伞柄被轻轻推入你的手中。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge plank sinking a finger's width under a truck, then rising back.
abstract.cn: 想象桥板在卡车下被压低一指宽，随后又回弹。

examples.en: The classmate gave his umbrella to his friend at the school gate.
examples.cn: 同桌在校门口把伞给了朋友。

examples.en: The head teacher gave a speech at the opening ceremony.
examples.cn: 校长在开学典礼上发表了演讲。

examples.en: The wooden bridge gives a little when trucks cross.
examples.cn: 木桥在卡车驶过时会轻微下弯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「给唔」——给东西时嘴里应一声「唔，拿好」；give 就是把东西递出去

root: give 源自日耳曼词根 gebhan（给予），古英语 giefan，过去式 gave、分词 given 为古形遗留；与 gift 同根，forgive 为其加前缀的形式。

sensesIntro.en: Give moves from the handed object to feelings, performances, yielding materials and letting go.
sensesIntro.cn: give 从递出的实物延伸到感觉、演出、材料的让步与放弃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand passing something forward
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的手把东西向前递出

intro.en: Give is a Germanic core verb; the items below are its endings and its compounds.
intro.cn: give 是日耳曼核心动词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare means to give; it is the Latin parallel family, not the source of give.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare 意为给予，是平行的拉丁词族，并非 give 的来源。

items.example: Old English giefan is the recorded base form.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 giefan 是有记录的基础形式。
for- 加 give 构成 forgive。

definition_zh: 高兴的；乐意的；令人高兴的
definition_en: pleased and happy about something, or willing to do something for someone
core_image: 脸上忽然亮起来的笑意：事情合了心意
scene: 收到录取通知的那天早晨，她一路小跑回了家。She was glad to hear that she had passed the exam.
sceneCN: 这里 glad 是「高兴的；欣慰的」（第 1 个义项：为某事感到愉快）；句意为她高兴地得知自己通过了考试。

pos.zh: 高兴的；乐意的；令人高兴的

derivatives.zh: 由 glad 加 -en 构成，义为「使高兴」
由 glad 加 -ly 构成，义为「乐意地」
由 glad 加 -ness 构成，义为「高兴；喜悦」

senses.title: Pleased about something
senses.definition: feeling pleased and happy because something has happened
senses.definitionCN: 因某事发生而感到愉快
senses.example: She was glad to hear that she had passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 她高兴地得知自己通过了考试。
senses.why: The core image is a face lighting up when things go your way, the plain everyday feeling.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是事情顺心时脸上亮起的神色，是最日常的情绪。

senses.title: Willing and ready to help
senses.definition: very willing to do something for someone
senses.definitionCN: 非常愿意为某人做某事
senses.example: I am glad to help you carry the boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 我很乐意帮你搬箱子。
senses.why: A happy heart says yes easily, so gladness slides into willingness.
senses.whyCN: 心情好的人 easily 点头，高兴便滑向乐意。

senses.title: Bringing joy to others
senses.definition: causing happiness to others, in older phrases like glad news or glad day
senses.definitionCN: 使他人快乐的，用于 glad news 等旧式表达
senses.example: The glad news spread through the village at once.
senses.exampleCN: 好消息立刻传遍了全村。
senses.why: The feeling a face shows can be given away, so events and news can be glad too.
senses.whyCN: 脸上的情绪可以传染给他人，于是消息与日子也可以是 glad 的。

senses.title: Bright and joyful in look
senses.definition: shining with joy, describing looks, eyes or sounds in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 闪耀喜悦光彩的，书面语中形容眼神、声音
senses.example: She welcomed them with glad eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她用欢悦的目光迎接他们。
senses.why: Joy is visible light on a face, so eyes and days can carry gladness like colour.
senses.whyCN: 喜悦像脸上的光，眼神与日子便都能带上这份亮色。

intro.en: Glad once meant bright and shining; happiness was imagined as light.
intro.cn: glad 曾意为明亮闪耀，快乐被想象成光。

items.en: The reconstructed root gladh- meant smooth and bright.
items.cn: 重构词根 gladh- 意为平滑、明亮。

items.en: Old English glæd meant bright, shining and also joyful.
items.cn: 古英语 glæd 意为明亮的，兼指喜悦的。

items.en: Middle English glad leaned toward the feeling of joy, keeping the bright metaphor.
items.cn: 中古英语 glad 偏向喜悦之情，保留了明亮的比喻。

items.en: Norse gladr, meaning bright and cheerful, is a close relative in the same family.
items.cn: 诺斯语 gladr 意为明快欢悦，是同族中的近亲。

items.en: Modern English settled glad on pleased and willing, while gladness and gladden survived.
items.cn: 现代英语把 glad 定在高兴与乐意，gladness 与 gladden 得以留存。

note.en: The words below sound like glad or share its field of happiness.
note.cn: 以下词与 glad 音近，或同属快乐义场。

entries.definition: An open space in a forest; one letter different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「林间空地」，与 glad 仅差一个字母，词义无关。

entries.definition: Willingly and happily.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「乐意地」，由 glad 直接派生。

entries.definition: Informal short for graduate; sounds close.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，graduates 的口语缩写，读音与 glad 接近。

entries.definition: Feeling or showing pleasure; the everyday general word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「快乐的」，最常用的日常说法。

entries.definition: Very pleased about something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「欣喜的」，程度比 glad 更强。

entries.definition: Happy in a way that shows in behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴高采烈的」，强调外显的情绪。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of glad.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Old English glæd meant bright as well as happy; joy was imagined as light.
normal.cn: 古英语 glæd 兼指明亮与快乐，喜悦被想象成光。

normal.en: German still has glatt for smooth, a cousin keeping the original sense.
normal.cn: 德语 glatt 意为光滑，保留了原始义的亲属词。

normal.en: Gladden is the verb that makes someone glad.
normal.cn: gladden 是使人高兴的动词。

normal.en: Glad to help is a polite set phrase in daily speech.
normal.cn: glad to help 是日常礼貌用语。

normal.en: Gladness is the noun for the state of being glad.
normal.cn: gladness 是 glad 的名词形式，指喜悦状态。

abstract.en: Picture a grey morning face turning bright the moment good news lands.
abstract.cn: 想象灰暗的晨脸在好消息落地的一瞬亮起来。

abstract.en: See a smile spread quickly before the mind even explains why.
abstract.cn: 想象笑容先于理由飞快展开。

abstract.en: Think of light sliding across a floor when a curtain is pulled open.
abstract.cn: 想象窗帘拉开时光线滑过地板。

examples.en: She was glad to hear that she had passed the exam.
examples.cn: 她高兴地得知自己通过了考试。

examples.en: I am glad to help you carry the boxes.
examples.cn: 我很乐意帮你搬箱子。

examples.en: The glad news spread through the village at once.
examples.cn: 好消息立刻传遍了全村。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哥拉的」——哥得到录取通知，乐得脸上放光；glad 读起来自带一声欢呼

root: glad 源自日耳曼词根 gladh-（平滑、明亮），古英语 glæd 兼指「明亮的」与「喜悦的」；德语同源词 glatt 仍保留「光滑」义。

sensesIntro.en: Glad runs from feeling pleased to being willing, giving joy and shining with it.
sensesIntro.cn: glad 从感到愉快延伸到乐意、给予快乐与散发光彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face lighting up when things go right
core.cn: 核心意象：事情顺心时脸上亮起的神采

intro.en: Glad is a Germanic base adjective; the items below are its endings and phrases.
intro.cn: glad 是日耳曼基础形容词，下面列出它的词尾与短语。

latinIntro.en: Latin laetus means joyful; it is the Latin parallel, not the source of glad.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laetus 意为喜悦的，是平行的拉丁词，并非 glad 的来源。

items.example: Old English glæd joined light and joy.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 glæd 连接光与喜悦。

definition_zh: 玻璃；玻璃杯；一杯之量；眼镜（复数）
definition_en: a hard transparent material, a drinking cup made of it, the amount it holds, or eyeglasses in the plural
core_image: 透明的硬片：能看穿却摸不着
scene: 厨房里，一杯牛奶被碰倒，透明的碎片溅到了地上。He picked up the broken glass from the kitchen floor.
sceneCN: 这里 glass 是「玻璃杯」（第 2 个义项：玻璃制的饮水容器）；句意为他从厨房地板上拾起碎玻璃杯。

pos.zh: 玻璃；玻璃杯；一杯之量；眼镜
给……装玻璃；把……做成玻璃状

derivatives.zh: 由 glass 加 -y 构成，义为「玻璃般的；呆滞的」
glass 与 ware 的复合词，义为「玻璃器皿」
eye 与 glass 的复合词，义为「镜片；眼镜」

senses.title: The hard transparent material
senses.definition: a hard, transparent substance used for windows, bottles and mirrors
senses.definitionCN: 用于窗、瓶、镜的坚硬透明材料
senses.example: The window glass shattered into small pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 窗玻璃碎成了小块。
senses.why: The core image is a clear, see-through solid, so the first sense is the material itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是透明可看穿的固体，所以第一义项就是材料本身。

senses.title: A drinking cup made of glass
senses.definition: a container for drinking, made of glass
senses.definitionCN: 玻璃制的饮用容器
senses.example: He picked up the broken glass from the kitchen floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他从厨房地板上拾起碎玻璃杯。
senses.why: The material is shaped into a cup, so the maker of cups borrows the material's name.
senses.whyCN: 材料被制成杯子，杯具便沿用材料的名字。

senses.title: The amount a glass holds
senses.definition: the quantity that a glass contains
senses.definitionCN: 一只玻璃杯所容的量
senses.example: She drank two glasses of juice at breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她早餐喝了两杯果汁。
senses.why: The cup measures what it carries, so the container becomes a unit of drink.
senses.whyCN: 杯子量出所盛之物，容器便成了计量单位。

senses.title: Eyeglasses
senses.definition: two lenses in a frame worn to see better, in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 戴在眼前帮助视力的双镜片，用复数
senses.example: Grandpa put on his glasses to read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 爷爷戴上眼镜读那封信。
senses.why: Two glass lenses sit before the eyes, so the pair of lenses takes the plural of the material.
senses.whyCN: 两片玻璃镜片置于眼前，成对的镜片便沿用材料的复数形式。

senses.title: To fit with glass or become glassy
senses.definition: to put glass into a frame, or to become glassy and dull-eyed
senses.definitionCN: 给框架装玻璃，或眼神变得呆滞发直
senses.example: The workers glassed the porch last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们去年春天给门廊装了玻璃。
senses.why: The material name turns into a verb when glass is put into something or eyes look like it.
senses.whyCN: 当玻璃被装进某物、或眼神像玻璃时，材料名便转为动词。

intro.en: Glass runs back to a Germanic word for the shining material itself.
intro.cn: glass 直接追溯到日耳曼语中指这种闪亮材料的词。

items.en: The reconstructed root glazam meant the transparent shining substance.
items.cn: 重构词根 glazam 意为透明的闪光物质。

items.en: Old English glæs meant glass, already the material and the cup.
items.cn: 古英语 glæs 意为玻璃，已兼指材料与杯具。

items.en: Norse gler, meaning shining glass, is a relative from the same family.
items.cn: 诺斯语 gler 意为闪亮的玻璃，是同族的亲属词。

items.en: Middle English glas settled the form and added the drink-measure use.
items.cn: 中古英语 glas 固定了词形，并增加了计饮量的用法。

items.en: Modern English spelled it glass and grew the eyeglasses and verb senses.
items.cn: 现代英语拼写定为 glass，并发展出眼镜义与动词用法。

note.en: The words below echo glass in sound or share its transparent world.
note.cn: 以下词与 glass 音近，或同属透明器物的世界。

entries.definition: A group of pupils or a category; differs by one letter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「班级；类别」，与 glass 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: Like glass in look; dull or smooth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「玻璃般的；呆滞的」，由 glass 直接派生。

entries.definition: A yellow metal alloy; rhymes with glass.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄铜」，与 glass 押韵，词义无关。

entries.definition: A small open container for drinking, often with a handle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杯子」，常带柄，不一定透明。

entries.definition: Clear colourless glass of fine quality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水晶玻璃」，指高品质透明玻璃。

entries.definition: A curved piece of glass for seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「镜片」，与 glasses 的核心部分相关。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of glass.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: German Glas and Dutch glas are twin forms of the same Germanic material word.
normal.cn: 德语 Glas 与荷兰语 glas 是同族材料词的双生形式。

normal.en: Glasses means two lenses, so the word is always plural for eyewear.
normal.cn: glasses 指两片镜片，指眼镜时总是复数。

normal.en: A glass of water counts the drink by the cup.
normal.cn: a glass of water 以杯计饮。

normal.en: Glassy describes eyes that shine but show no feeling.
normal.cn: glassy 形容有光泽却无神采的眼神。

normal.en: Glasshouse is a building of glass for growing plants.
normal.cn: glasshouse 指种植物的玻璃房。

abstract.en: Picture rain sliding down a window while you watch the street through it.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水滑过窗玻璃，你透过它望着街道。

abstract.en: See a drinking glass turn empty, leaving a ring of water on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃杯被喝空，桌上留下一圈水痕。

abstract.en: Think of shattered pieces catching sunlight on the floor.
abstract.cn: 想象碎片在地板上反射阳光。

examples.en: He picked up the broken glass from the kitchen floor.
examples.cn: 他从厨房地板上拾起碎玻璃杯。

examples.en: Grandpa put on his glasses to read the letter.
examples.cn: 爷爷戴上眼镜读那封信。

examples.en: She drank two glasses of juice at breakfast.
examples.cn: 她早餐喝了两杯果汁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格拉斯」——隔着透明的格挡看东西，那层「拉」不开的就是玻璃；glass 让人想到透明的窗

root: glass 源自日耳曼词根 glazam（透明闪亮的物质），古英语 glæs；与德语 Glas、荷兰语 glas 同源，属纯日耳曼词族。

sensesIntro.en: Glass moves from the material to the cup, the measure, the lenses and finally the verb.
sensesIntro.cn: glass 从材料延伸到杯子、计量、镜片，最后转为动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clear solid you can see straight through
core.cn: 核心意象：可以一眼看穿的透明固体

intro.en: Glass is a Germanic base noun; the items below are its endings and compounds.
intro.cn: glass 是日耳曼基础名词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vitrum means glass; it is the Latin parallel, not the source of glass.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vitrum 意为玻璃，是平行的拉丁词，并非 glass 的来源。

items.example: Old English glæs named the material first.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 glæs 最早指这种材料。

definition_zh: 手套；（棒球、拳击等的）手套装具
definition_en: a covering worn on the hand to protect or warm it, or a padded mitt used in sports
core_image: 套在手上的保护壳：五指各有归处
scene: 冬天的清晨，出门前妈妈把一副毛线手套塞进孩子口袋。She pulled on her wool gloves before stepping into the snow.
sceneCN: 这里 glove 是「手套」（第 1 个义项：护手保暖之物）；句意为她在走进雪地前戴上了毛线手套。

derivatives.zh: 由 glove 加 -ed 构成，义为「戴着手套的」
glove 与 box 的复合词，义为「（车内）杂物箱」
连指手套，与 glove 同义场但五指不分

senses.title: A hand covering
senses.definition: a shaped covering for the hand, with a separate part for each finger
senses.definitionCN: 分指包覆整只手的套具
senses.example: She pulled on her wool gloves before stepping into the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 她在走进雪地前戴上了毛线手套。
senses.why: The core image is a second skin for the hand, so the plain sense is the covering itself.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是手的第二层皮肤，最直接的义项就是护手之物。

senses.title: A sports mitt
senses.definition: a padded or webbed glove used in baseball, boxing or golf
senses.definitionCN: 棒球、拳击或高尔夫用的加厚套具
senses.example: The catcher caught the ball in his glove.
senses.exampleCN: 捕手用手套接住了球。
senses.why: Protection is pushed further for sport, where the glove must absorb hard blows.
senses.whyCN: 保护功能在运动中加强，手套须能吸收重击。

senses.title: A symbol of challenge or honour
senses.titleCN: 手套式的挑战象征；荣誉标记
senses.definition: a glove thrown down as a challenge, or one sent as a pledge in old custom
senses.definitionCN: 旧俗中掷下手套表示挑战，或送手套为信物
senses.example: The knight threw down his glove in challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士掷下手套发出挑战。
senses.why: The hand-covering stands for its owner's hand, so throwing it stands for a raised fist.
senses.whyCN: 手套代表主人的手，掷出手套便等于举起拳头。

senses.title: To cover with a glove
senses.definition: to put a glove on, or to catch something with a gloved hand
senses.definitionCN: 戴上手套，或用戴手套的手接住
senses.example: The keeper gloved the ball safely in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员在雨中稳稳地用手套装住了球。
senses.why: The noun names the action it makes possible: the covering goes onto the hand.
senses.whyCN: 名词转指它所实现的行为：套具被套上手。

senses.title: A tight-fitting fit
senses.definition: a fit as close as a glove, in the phrase fit like a glove
senses.definitionCN: 形容衣物贴合如手套，用于 fit like a glove
senses.example: The new coat fits like a glove.
senses.exampleCN: 新大衣非常合身。
senses.why: A glove hugs every finger exactly, so perfect fit borrows its name.
senses.whyCN: 手套紧贴每一根手指，完美贴合便借用其名。

intro.en: Glove's history is uncertain, but its Germanic family is clear.
intro.cn: glove 的词源细节不确定，但其日耳曼词族脉络清晰。

items.en: The exact source is uncertain; the word is confined to Germanic languages.
items.cn: 确切来源不确定，该词只见于日耳曼语。

items.en: Old English glof meant a covering for the hand.
items.cn: 古英语 glof 意为护手之物。

items.en: Norse gaumi and related forms are cousins in the same hand-covering family.
items.cn: 诺斯语 gaumi 等形式是同族的手套亲属词。

items.en: Middle English spelled it glove, and the challenge custom gave it a symbolic use.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 glove，掷手套习俗赋予它象征用法。

items.en: Modern English added the sports mitt and the verb uses.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了运动套具义与动词用法。

note.en: The words below sound close to glove or live in the hand-covering field.
note.cn: 以下词与 glove 音近，或同属护手物件义场。

entries.definition: A small storage box in a car.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「车内杂物箱」，glove 的复合词。

entries.definition: The earth or a round model of it; two letters differ.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地球仪；球体」，拼写与 glove 相近，词义无关。

entries.definition: Dried flower buds used as a spice; sounds close.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丁香（香料）」，读音与 gloves 接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A hand covering with one space for all fingers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「连指手套」，四指并拢不分。

entries.definition: An armoured or long glove.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「防护长手套」，旧时骑士装具。

entries.definition: A short glove or a baseball mitt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「短手套；棒球手套」，口语用法。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of glove.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Old English glof covered the hand long before sports existed.
normal.cn: 古英语 glof 在运动出现之前就护手了。

normal.en: Fit like a glove describes clothing that hugs every part.
normal.cn: fit like a glove 形容衣物处处贴合。

normal.en: To throw down the glove was the medieval way to challenge someone.
normal.cn: 掷下手套是中世纪下战书的方式。

normal.en: A boxing glove is padded to soften hard punches.
normal.cn: 拳击手套填了衬垫以缓和重击。

normal.en: Oven gloves protect the hand from hot dishes.
normal.cn: oven gloves 保护手免受热烫。

abstract.en: Picture five fingers sliding into five warm pockets.
abstract.cn: 想象五根手指滑进五个温暖的指套。

abstract.en: See snow falling on a red wool glove held out to catch it.
abstract.cn: 想象雪落在伸出去接雪的红色毛线手套上。

abstract.en: Think of a glove thrown to the floor between two staring knights.
abstract.cn: 想象两只对视的骑士之间一只手套掷落在地。

examples.en: She pulled on her wool gloves before stepping into the snow.
examples.cn: 她在走进雪地前戴上了毛线手套。

examples.en: The catcher caught the ball in his glove.
examples.cn: 捕手用手套接住了球。

examples.en: The new coat fits like a glove.
examples.cn: 新大衣非常合身。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格拉夫」——五根手指各有各的「窝」，套上它寒冷抓不住手；glove 与 love 只差一个字母，冬天里手也需要爱

sensesIntro.en: Glove stretches from the warm hand-covering to sports gear, challenge signs and the perfect fit.
sensesIntro.cn: glove 从保暖护手延伸到运动装具、挑战信物与完美贴合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second skin fitted over the hand
core.cn: 核心意象：套在手上如第二层皮肤的护具

intro.en: Glove is a Germanic base noun; the items below are its endings and compounds.
intro.cn: glove 是日耳曼基础名词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin manuca means a hand-covering; it is the Latin parallel, not the source of glove.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manuca 意为护手套，是平行的拉丁词，并非 glove 的来源。

items.example: Old English glof named the covering.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 glof 指护手之物。

items.example: It forms fit like a glove.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 fit like a glove。

definition_zh: 胶水；胶黏物；胶合；紧贴不舍（作动词）
definition_en: a sticky substance that joins things, or to fasten things with it; figuratively, to keep eyes fixed on something
core_image: 黏住不放的透明液体：把两样东西硬连在一起
scene: 手工课上，两张彩纸被一片一片粘成了风车。The pupils glued the paper pieces onto the wheel.
sceneCN: 这里 glue 是「用胶水粘贴」（第 2 个义项：把东西黏合）；句意为学生们把纸片粘到风车上。

derivatives.zh: 由 glue 加 -y 构成，义为「胶黏的」
由 glue 加 -y 构成，义为「黏糊糊的」
super 与 glue 的复合词，义为「强力胶」

senses.title: A sticky joining substance
senses.definition: a thick sticky liquid or paste used for joining surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 用于黏合表面的黏稠液体或膏体
senses.example: A drop of glue sealed the torn page.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴胶水把撕坏的书页封好了。
senses.why: The core image is a liquid that grips two things so hard they will not part.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把两样东西黏得拆不开的液体。

senses.title: To fasten with glue
senses.definition: to join things together using glue
senses.definitionCN: 用胶水把东西连在一起
senses.example: The pupils glued the paper pieces onto the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们把纸片粘到风车上。
senses.why: The substance turns into the action: the stickiness does the joining.
senses.whyCN: 物质转为动作：靠黏性完成连接。

senses.title: To fix eyes or attention
senses.definition: to keep eyes or attention firmly fixed on something
senses.definitionCN: 使眼睛或注意力牢牢锁定某物
senses.example: The children were glued to the cartoon show.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们目不转睛地看动画片。
senses.why: What glue does to paper, fascination does to the eyes: they cannot leave.
senses.whyCN: 胶水对纸做的事，吸引对眼睛做的事：离不开。

senses.title: Any bonding agent
senses.definition: any substance or force that holds parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分连结起来的任何物质或力量
senses.example: Shared memories are the glue of the old friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的回忆是这段老友谊的黏合剂。
senses.why: Anything that keeps a group from falling apart is called glue.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能把群体维系在一起的东西都可以被称为 glue。

senses.title: A sticky residue or smear
senses.definition: sticky matter left on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 留在表面的黏腻残留
senses.example: There is still some glue on the back of the sticker.
senses.exampleCN: 贴纸背面还留着些胶。
senses.why: Glue clings even when its job is done, so traces of it count as glue.
senses.whyCN: 黏性在任务完成后仍不放手，残留痕迹也被称为 glue。

intro.en: Glue comes from the Latin word for the sticky stuff made from animal hides.
intro.cn: glue 源自拉丁语中指兽皮熬制黏胶的词。

items.en: Latin gluten meant glue, the sticky substance boiled from hides and bones.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gluten 意为黏胶，由兽皮与骨头熬成。

items.en: Medieval Latin glua kept the sticky sense through scholarship.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 glua 在学术传统中保留黏着义。

items.en: Old French glu carried the word into Romance speech.
items.cn: 古法语 glu 把这个词带入罗曼语世界。

items.en: Middle English took glue from French for the sticky paste.
items.cn: 中古英语从法语借入 glue，指黏膏。

items.en: Modern English generalized glue to any adhesive and to fixed attention.
items.cn: 现代英语把 glue 扩展为一切黏合剂，并引申为紧贴的注意力。

note.en: The words below sound like glue or share its sticky field.
note.cn: 以下词与 glue 音近，或同属黏着义场。

entries.definition: Sticky like glue.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「胶黏的」，由 glue 直接派生。

entries.definition: To fill beyond need; one letter differs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使饱足；充斥」，与 glue 拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The colour of the sky; rhymes with glue.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「蓝色的」，与 glue 押韵，词义无关。

entries.definition: A soft sticky mixture for sticking things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「糨糊」，偏软性黏合材料。

entries.definition: A substance used for sticking; more technical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黏合剂」，偏技术与工业用语。

entries.definition: To cling or attach by sticking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「粘住；钉住」，与 glue 的动词义相近。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of glue.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Latin gluten is also the name of the sticky protein in wheat.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 gluten 也是小麦中黏性蛋白的名字，即面筋。

normal.en: Glued to the screen keeps the sticky picture for attention.
normal.cn: glued to the screen 用黏住的画面形容注意力。

normal.en: A glue stick is glue shaped like a lipstick tube.
normal.cn: glue stick 是做成唇膏管状的固体胶。

normal.en: Superglue is the strongest everyday adhesive.
normal.cn: superglue 是日常最强的黏合剂。

normal.en: French glu and Italian glutine keep the old Latin family alive.
normal.cn: 法语 glu 与意大利语 glutine 延续了古拉丁词族。

abstract.en: Picture two fingers slowly pulling apart with thin sticky threads between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两根手指慢慢分开，中间拉着黏丝。

abstract.en: See a torn comic page pressed flat and holding again.
abstract.cn: 想象撕破的漫画页被压平重新粘牢。

abstract.en: Think of eyes pinned to a screen, unable to look away.
abstract.cn: 想象眼睛钉在屏幕上，挪不开视线。

examples.en: The pupils glued the paper pieces onto the wheel.
examples.cn: 学生们把纸片粘到风车上。

examples.en: The children were glued to the cartoon show.
examples.cn: 孩子们目不转睛地看动画片。

examples.en: Shared memories are the glue of the old friendship.
examples.cn: 共同的回忆是这段老友谊的黏合剂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「固噜」——涂上它东西就固定得「噜」不开；glue 黏住就不放，像响亮的一声粘合

root: glue 源自拉丁语 gluten（黏胶，兽皮熬制），经中世纪拉丁语 glua、古法语 glu 传入英语；gluten（面筋）为同源词。

sensesIntro.en: Glue runs from the sticky substance to the joining action and the eyes that cannot look away.
sensesIntro.cn: glue 从黏稠物质延伸到黏合动作，再到无法移开的目光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sticky film that refuses to let go
core.cn: 核心意象：黏住不放的薄膜

intro.en: Glue is a borrowed base; the items below are its endings and compounds.
intro.cn: glue 是借入的基础词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gluten is the direct ancestor, so the Latin family is glue's own family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gluten 是直接祖先，因此拉丁词族就是 glue 本族。

items.example: Middle English borrowed glue from French.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语从法语借入 glue。

definition_zh: 去；前往；进行；运转；变得；离开
definition_en: to move or travel from one place to another, to proceed or function, or to change into a state
core_image: 迈出去的脚步：人从原地走向别处
scene: 放学铃一响，孩子们背起书包朝校门走去。The pupils go home by bus after school.
sceneCN: 这里 go 是「前往；去」（第 1 个义项：从一处移到另一处）；句意为放学后学生们乘公交回家。

derivatives.zh: 由 go 加 -ing 构成，义为「出发；进行状况」
由 go 加 -er 构成，义为「常去的人；出走者」
on 与 go 的复合词，义为「进行中的」

senses.title: To move or travel to a place
senses.definition: to move or travel from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方移动或行进到另一个地方
senses.example: The pupils go home by bus after school.
senses.exampleCN: 放学后学生们乘公交回家。
senses.why: The core image is a step that leaves the starting spot, the plainest movement.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是离开原地的一步，是最基本的移动。

senses.title: To proceed or function
senses.definition: to happen or to work in a certain way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式发生或运作
senses.example: How did your interview go this morning?
senses.exampleCN: 你今天上午的面试进行得怎么样？
senses.why: A journey has a course, so an event or a machine also has a way it goes.
senses.whyCN: 旅程有进程，事情与机器也有各自的运转方式。

senses.title: To change into a state
senses.definition: to enter a certain condition, often a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 进入某种状态，常指变坏
senses.example: The milk went sour in the warm kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶在温暖的厨房里变酸了。
senses.why: Going somewhere can be going into a new condition: the step lands in a different state.
senses.whyCN: 走向某处也可以是走入新状态：脚步落进了另一种情形。

senses.title: To leave or disappear
senses.definition: to depart, or to stop existing or working
senses.definitionCN: 离去，或不再存在、不再运作
senses.example: The lights went out during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨中灯灭了。
senses.why: A step away becomes a disappearance: what went is no longer there.
senses.whyCN: 一步离去即成消失：走了的便不在了。

senses.title: A turn or attempt
senses.definition: one person's turn to act, or an attempt at something
senses.definitionCN: 轮到某人行动的一次，或一次尝试
senses.example: It is your go to roll the dice.
senses.exampleCN: 轮到你掷骰子了。
senses.why: Each moving person takes a step in order, so a turn is one going.
senses.whyCN: 依次行动的人各走一步，一次轮替就是一次 go。

intro.en: Go is one of English's oldest verbs, with a past tense borrowed from a different verb family.
intro.cn: go 是英语最古老的动词之一，其过去式来自另一个动词家族。

items.en: Old English gan meant to go; the participle geganges survives in gang.
items.cn: 古英语 gan 意为去，分词 geganges 的痕迹留存在 gang。

items.en: The past tense went came from wend, through Norse influence on Old English.
items.cn: 过去式 went 来自 wend，受诺斯语影响混入。

items.en: The root ghan- also gave German gehen and Dutch gaan, close cousins of go.
items.cn: 词根 ghan- 也派生了德语 gehen 与荷兰语 gaan，是 go 的近亲。

items.en: Middle English fixed go for the present and went for the past, a mixed pair.
items.cn: 中古英语固定 go 为现在式、went 为过去式，成为混合配对。

items.en: Modern English built on go the huge family of phrasal uses like go on and go out.
items.cn: 现代英语发展出 go on、go out 等大量短语用法。

note.en: The words below echo go in sound or share the movement field.
note.cn: 以下词与 go 音近，或同属移动义场。

entries.definition: A deity; one letter different.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神」，与 go 仅差一个字母，词义无关。

entries.definition: An aim or a scored point; sounds close.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标；进球」，读音与 go 接近。

entries.definition: Third-person singular of go.
entries.definitionCN: goes 是 go 的三单形式。

entries.definition: To change position or place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「移动」，强调位置变化。

entries.definition: To go away from a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「离开」，强调脱离原地。

entries.definition: To make a journey, especially a long one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「旅行」，多指较远路程。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of go.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Went is not go's own past; it was stolen from the verb wend.
normal.cn: went 并非 go 的本族过去式，而是从 wend 借来的。

normal.en: German gehen and Dutch gaan are close cousins of go.
normal.cn: 德语 gehen 与荷兰语 gaan 是 go 的近亲。

normal.en: Go bad and go sour use go for entering a new state.
normal.cn: go bad 与 go sour 用 go 表示进入新状态。

normal.en: Have a go means try it once, in British speech.
normal.cn: have a go 在英式口语里指试一次。

normal.en: Ongoing means still moving forward, not finished.
normal.cn: ongoing 指仍在推进、未结束。

abstract.en: Picture one foot lifting off the ground and landing ahead of the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚抬起、落在另一只脚前方。

abstract.en: See a school gate swinging open as children stream through.
abstract.cn: 想象校门敞开，孩子们涌出门去。

abstract.en: Think of a light switching itself off in an empty room.
abstract.cn: 想象空房间里灯自行熄灭。

examples.en: The pupils go home by bus after school.
examples.cn: 放学后学生们乘公交回家。

examples.en: The milk went sour in the warm kitchen.
examples.cn: 牛奶在温暖的厨房里变酸了。

examples.cn: 轮到你掷骰子了。

sensesIntro.en: Go runs from physical movement to how things proceed, states entered, departures and turns.
sensesIntro.cn: go 从身体的移动延伸到事情的进行、进入的状态、离去与轮替。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step that leaves the starting place
core.cn: 核心意象：离开原地的一步

intro.cn: go 是日耳曼核心动词，下面列出它的词尾与短语搭档。

latinIntro.en: Latin ire means to go; it is the Latin parallel, not the source of go.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ire 意为去，是平行的拉丁词，并非 go 的来源。

definition_zh: 目标；目的；球门；进球得分；终点
definition_en: the end point you aim at, whether a line to cross, a result to achieve, or a frame to put the ball into
core_image: 跑道尽头插着的一面旗，所有脚步都朝它收拢
scene: 决赛的最后时刻，前锋一脚把球踢进了球门。She scored the winning goal in the last minute of the match.
sceneCN: 这里 goal 是「进球、得分」（第 4 个义项：把球送进球门所得到的一分）；句意：她在比赛最后一分钟打入了制胜的一球。场景要点：球门网、飞过门线的球、停在最后一分钟的计时器，以及看台上举起的手臂。

derivatives.zh: 守门员
守门员

没有进球的

senses.title: The end point of a race
senses.definition: the mark or line at which a race ends
senses.definitionCN: 赛跑结束处的标记或界线
senses.example: The runners sprinted toward the goal at the far end of the track.
senses.exampleCN: 选手们朝跑道尽头的终点冲刺。
senses.why: Goal is first recorded in the 1530s as the end point of a race. The word names the mark that ends motion, and its own origin is not settled.
senses.whyCN: goal 最早在 16 世纪 30 年代记录为赛跑的终点。这个词命名的是让运动结束的那个标记，而它自身的来源尚无定论。

senses.title: The object of an effort
senses.definition: the result or state that a person or group works toward
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体努力要达成的结果或状态
senses.example: Her goal is to finish the marathon under four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她的目标是在四小时内跑完马拉松。
senses.why: The figurative sense, also from the 1540s, treats life as a course: the result you want is the mark you run toward.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻义同样始于 16 世纪 40 年代：它把人生当作一段赛程，你想要的结果就是你朝它奔跑的那个标记。

senses.title: The frame where the ball is put
senses.definition: the structure of posts and net into which players try to send the ball
senses.definitionCN: 由门柱和球网构成、球员努力把球送进去的结构
senses.example: The goalkeeper stood between the posts of the goal.
senses.exampleCN: 守门员站在球门柱之间。
senses.why: The sports sense, also from the 1540s, makes the end point physical: a frame marks the place where the ball must arrive.
senses.whyCN: 同样始于 16 世纪 40 年代的体育义项，把终点变成实物：一个框架标出了球必须抵达的位置。

senses.title: A score made in the frame
senses.definition: a point gained by sending the ball through or into the goal
senses.definitionCN: 把球送过门线或送进球门而得到的一分
senses.example: She scored the winning goal in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一分钟打入了制胜的一球。
senses.why: By metonymy the frame gives its name to the event of putting the ball through it: the endpoint becomes the point gained.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，框架把自己的名字借给了“把球送进去”这件事：终点变成了所得的一分。

senses.title: A measured target in work
senses.definition: a figure or quota that a team or company is expected to reach
senses.definitionCN: 团队或公司被要求达到的数字或定额
senses.example: The sales team missed its quarterly goal by two percent.
senses.exampleCN: 销售团队以两个百分点的差距未能达到季度指标。
senses.why: A number can serve as the mark: once the target is measurable, the race endpoint becomes a quota.
senses.whyCN: 数字也可以充当那个标记：一旦目标可以计量，赛跑的终点就变成了定额。

senses.title: A long-term aim in life
senses.definition: a distant aim that gives direction to a person's life or career
senses.definitionCN: 为人生或事业提供方向的远期追求
senses.example: His goal is to run a clinic in his home town.
senses.exampleCN: 他的志向是在家乡开一家诊所。
senses.why: The largest version of the same image: a whole life is the course, and one distant mark gives it direction.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一个意象的最大版本：整个人生是赛程，一个远处的标记为它提供方向。

senses.title: Own goal: a score against your own side
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase own goal, a goal scored accidentally for the opposing team
senses.definitionCN: 在固定搭配 own goal 中，指误为对方球队打进的一球
senses.example: The defender's own goal decided the tie.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫的乌龙球决定了这场平局的结果。
senses.why: The frame is neutral: a ball put into the wrong one still counts. English names that accident with the fixed phrase own goal.
senses.whyCN: 球门本身是中立的：球进了错误的那一个，仍然算数。英语用固定说法 own goal 命名这种意外。

senses.title: Goal line and goal area
senses.definition: the line and the marked area on the field that belong to the goal
senses.definitionCN: 场地上属于球门的那条线和被划出的区域
senses.example: The ball crossed the goal line by a few centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 球越过球门线几厘米。
senses.why: The frame projects a boundary onto the field; the line and the area are the ground version of the same endpoint.
senses.whyCN: 球门把一条边界投射到场地上；球门线与球门区是同一个终点在地面上的版本。

senses.title: Attributive: goal-directed, goal-setting
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe activity organised around a target
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一名词之前，描述围绕目标组织起来的活动
senses.example: Goal-setting theory treats clear targets as a motivator.
senses.exampleCN: 目标设定理论把清晰的目标视为一种激励因素。
senses.why: When the word moves in front of another noun, it stops naming a mark and starts labelling the activity that is organised around one.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词移到另一个名词前面时，它不再命名一个标记，而是给围绕某个标记组织起来的活动贴标签。

intro.en: Goal is a single noun of uncertain origin: it appears in the 1530s as the end of a race, and every later sense keeps that 'mark ahead' shape.
intro.cn: goal 是一个来源不确定的单词：它在 16 世纪 30 年代以“赛跑终点”出现，后来每个义项都保留着“前方有一个标记”的形状。

items.en: First recorded as 'end point of a race'. The word appears once earlier, as gol in an early-14c poem, with an apparent sense of 'boundary, limit'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“赛跑的终点”。这个词更早还出现过一次，在 14 世纪早期的一首诗里写作 gol，似乎是“边界、界限”的意思。

items.en: Three origins have been proposed and none is established: Old English *gal 'obstacle, barrier', implied by gælan 'to hinder' and by compounds such as singal and widgal; Old Norse geil 'a narrow glen, a passage'; or Old French gaule 'long pole, stake', which is Germanic in origin. The source is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 先后有三种来源被提出，但没有一种得到确认：一是古英语 *gal“障碍、壁垒”，由 gælan“阻碍”以及 singal、widgal 等复合词推知；二是古诺尔斯语 geil“狭窄峡谷、通道”；三是古法语 gaule“长杆、桩”，而后者本身出自日耳曼语。词源属于存疑。

items.en: The sports sense 'place where the ball is put to score' is recorded, and in the same decade the figurative sense 'object of an effort'.
items.cn: 记录到体育义“把球放进去得分的位置”，同一时期还出现比喻义“努力的目标”。

items.en: Goal-keeper appears in the 1650s; field goal in 1889; goal-tender in 1889; goalie in 1921 as a shortening of goal-tender.
items.cn: goal-keeper 出现于 17 世纪 50 年代；field goal 与 goal-tender 出现于 1889 年；goalie 于 1921 年作为 goal-tender 的缩略形式出现。

items.en: Goalpost, goal line, goal area, own goal and goalless fill out the family. Goal itself remains a noun only; there is no verb 'to goal' in standard English.
items.cn: goalpost、goal line、goal area、own goal、goalless 补全了这一词族。goal 本身始终只是名词；标准英语中没有 to goal 这样的动词用法。

items.en: Gold is a different word with a different history; the resemblance to goal is only in sound and spelling. German Ziel means 'goal, target' but is not the source of the English word.
items.cn: gold 是另一个词，来历完全不同；它与 goal 的相似只在读音和拼写上。德语 Ziel 意为“目标、终点”，但它并不是英语这个词的来源。

note.en: The first group is sound and spelling neighbours, including two that merely look like goal; the second compares the words for what you are trying to reach.
note.cn: 第一组是读音与拼写上的邻居，其中两个只是看起来像 goal；第二组比较表示“你想要抵达的东西”的几个词。

entries.definition: the yellow metal. It has no historical link with goal; only the vowel and the final consonant resemble each other.
entries.definitionCN: 那种黄色金属。它与 goal 没有任何历史联系，只是元音和结尾辅音相近。

entries.definition: one of the two uprights of a goal. It is a compound of goal plus post, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 球门两根立柱之一。它是 goal 加 post 的合成词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: a goalkeeper. It is a 1921 shortening of goal-tender, so it belongs to the goal family.
entries.definitionCN: 守门员。它是 1921 年对 goal-tender 的缩略，因此属于 goal 词族。

entries.definition: without a goal being scored, as in a goalless draw. The suffix -less marks absence, not a new sense.
entries.definitionCN: 没有进球的，如 goalless draw。后缀 -less 标记“没有”，并不产生新义项。

entries.definition: what you intend to achieve; also the act of pointing at something. It is close to goal but often more personal and less measurable.
entries.definitionCN: 你打算达成的东西；也指瞄准的动作。它与 goal 接近，但往往更个人化、更不可量化。

entries.definition: a specific result that an organisation formally sets out to achieve. It is more formal and more measurable than goal.
entries.definitionCN: 组织正式设定要达成的具体结果。它比 goal 更正式、更可量化。

entries.definition: a level or figure to be reached, often with a deadline. It stresses the number to hit, while goal stresses the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 需要达到的水平或数字，常带截止时间。它强调要命中的数字，而 goal 强调方向。

entries.definition: the reason something exists or is done. It answers 'why', while goal answers 'where to'.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在或被做的理由。它回答“为什么”，而 goal 回答“往哪里去”。

normalIntro.en: Real word parts and real relatives: the noun goal, its compounds goalpost and goalkeeper, and the 1921 shortening goalie.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构词成分与真实同族词：名词 goal，它的合成词 goalpost、goalkeeper，以及 1921 年的缩略形式 goalie。

normal.en: Goal first meant the end of a race: a mark you run toward.
normal.cn: goal 最初指赛跑的终点：一个你朝它奔跑的标记。

normal.en: The sports frame is that same mark made visible, and the score is named after the frame.
normal.cn: 体育中的球门就是同一个标记变成实物，而“得分”又被球门命名。

normal.en: Gold and goal are only neighbours in sound; they have no shared history.
normal.cn: gold 与 goal 只是读音上的邻居，没有共同的来历。

normal.en: Own goal is a fixed phrase: the ball goes into the frame, but the wrong one.
normal.cn: own goal 是固定说法：球确实进了门，只是进错了那一个。

normal.en: Goal-setting and goal-directed show the noun working as a modifier, common in psychology and management.
normal.cn: goal-setting 与 goal-directed 显示这个名词可以作修饰语，这在心理学与管理学中很常见。

abstract.en: Picture a flag at the end of a track: every lane converges on it.
abstract.cn: 想象跑道尽头插着一面旗：每一条跑道都朝它收拢。

abstract.en: The flag can be a line, a number, a frame or a distant plan; the word always points to one mark.
abstract.cn: 那面旗可以是一条线、一个数字、一个框架，或一个远期的计划；这个词始终指向同一个标记。

abstract.en: A goal is not the running; it is the place where the running stops being open.
abstract.cn: 目标不是奔跑本身；它是奔跑不再敞开的那一点。

examples.en: The team's goal is to cut water use by a third within five years.
examples.cn: 这个团队的目标是在五年内把用水量削减三分之一。

examples.en: He scored twice and set up the third goal.
examples.cn: 他打进两球，并助攻了第三个进球。

examples.en: Without a clear goal, the meetings drifted from topic to topic.
examples.cn: 没有明确的目标，会议就从一个话题漂到另一个话题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “够儿”——一路跑到尽头，够着那面旗儿 → goal 目标、终点（只借音，不表词源）

root: 词源存疑：最早指赛跑的终点（1530 年代），可能来自古英语表示“障碍、界限”的词或古法语“长杆”；核心是“所有努力都朝向的那个终点”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of goal, all built on one position: a mark placed ahead, which motion or effort is organised to reach.
sensesIntro.cn: goal 的九个义项都建立在同一个位置关系上：前方放着一个标记，运动或努力都围绕抵达它来组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark ahead that every step converges on.
core.cn: 核心意象：前方的一个标记，所有脚步都朝它收拢。

branches.en: RACE: the original sense is the physical end point of a course.
branches.cn: 赛跑：最初的义项就是赛程的物理终点。

branches.en: AIM: the mark becomes mental, from a single task to a whole life's direction.
branches.cn: 目标：标记变成心里的，从一项任务一直到整个人生的方向。

branches.en: FRAME: in sport the mark is built of posts and line, a place the ball must reach.
branches.cn: 球门：在体育中，标记由门柱与门线构成，是球必须抵达的位置。

branches.en: SCORE: the frame lends its name to the point, including the accidental own goal.
branches.cn: 得分：球门把名字借给那一分，也包括意外的乌龙球。

branches.en: MEASURE: a number can be the mark, and the noun can label activity organised around it.
branches.cn: 计量：数字可以成为标记，这个名词也能给围绕标记组织的活动贴标签。

intro.en: Goal is not built from prefixes or suffixes; it is one noun whose family is made of compounds and a few endings such as -ie, -less and the plural -s.
intro.cn: goal 不是由前缀或后缀构成的；它是一个单词名词，其词族由合成词和 -ie、-less、复数 -s 等少数词尾组成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is known. The word appears in English in the 1530s with an uncertain origin, and the three candidates are Old English, Old Norse and Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 没有已知的拉丁语来源。这个词在 16 世纪 30 年代出现于英语，来源不确定，三个候选分别来自古英语、古诺尔斯语与古法语。

items.meaning: an end point, aim, or frame for scoring
items.example: The goal is to finish before noon.
items.exampleCN: 目标是在中午之前完成。

items.meaningCN: 多个目标；多个进球（复数）
items.example: The team has scored nine goals this season.
items.exampleCN: 这支球队本赛季已打进九球。

items.meaningCN: 没有进球的（-less 表示“没有”）
守门员（-ie 构成亲昵缩略）

items.meaning: the player who guards the goal
items.example: The goalkeeper punched the ball clear.

items.meaning: one of the uprights of a goal

items.example: The ball rolled over the goal line.

items.meaning: the marked area in front of the goal
items.example: The foul happened inside the goal area.
items.exampleCN: 那次犯规发生在球门区内。

items.meaning: a goal scored accidentally against one's own team
items.example: His own goal put the visitors ahead.
items.exampleCN: 他的乌龙球让客队领先。

items.meaning: a score made from the playing field, as in football
items.meaningCN: 射门得分（美式足球等的场上得分）
items.example: They won with a field goal in the final seconds.
items.exampleCN: 他们在最后几秒靠一次射门得分赢下比赛。

definition_zh: 神；上帝；神像；极受崇拜的人
definition_en: a being worshipped as having special powers over the world, or a person admired intensely
core_image: 高处的存在：掌控世界、被人仰望敬拜
scene: 古庙里，人们对着神像低头合掌祈愿。People prayed to their gods at the old temple.
sceneCN: 这里 god 是「神；神像」（第 1 个义项：被敬拜的超自然存在）；句意为人们在古庙向他们的神祈祷。

pos.zh: 神；上帝；神像；偶像般的人物

senses.title: A being worshipped
senses.definition: a superhuman being or image worshipped as having power over nature
senses.definitionCN: 被敬拜、被认为能左右自然的超人存在或其形象
senses.example: People prayed to their gods at the old temple.
senses.exampleCN: 人们在古庙向他们的神祈祷。
senses.why: The core image is something above humans that controls the world, so the plain sense is the worshipped being.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是凌驾于人、掌控世界的存在，最基本的义项就是被敬拜的对象。

senses.title: God as the one supreme being
senses.definition: the one all-powerful creator, written with a capital letter
senses.definitionCN: 全知全能的唯一造物主，首字母大写
senses.example: She thanks God for her family's safety.
senses.exampleCN: 她感谢上帝保佑全家平安。
senses.why: When many powers shrink to one, the word is raised and capitalized as the single God.
senses.whyCN: 当众神归于一神，词形随之抬升、大写，指唯一的上帝。

senses.title: An image or idol
senses.definition: a carved image treated as a god
senses.definitionCN: 被视为神的雕刻形象
senses.example: The wooden god stood in the shrine.
senses.exampleCN: 木制神像立在神龛里。
senses.why: The invisible being is given a visible body, so the image carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 无形的神被赋予可见的身体，形象便继承了名字。

senses.title: An intensely admired person
senses.definition: a person admired so much that others treat them like a deity
senses.definitionCN: 被崇拜到近乎神明的人
senses.example: Teenagers treated the singer as a pop god.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年把那位歌手当作流行乐之神。
senses.why: Worship keeps its shape even when the object is human, so admired people become gods.
senses.whyCN: 敬拜的形态保留，即使对象换成人，被膜拜的名人便成了 god。

senses.title: A supreme example
senses.definition: something regarded as the ultimate in its kind
senses.definitionCN: 某类事物中的极致代表
senses.example: This bakery is the god of all breakfast shops in town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店是全镇早餐店的翘楚。
senses.why: The power to rule becomes the power to excel, so the best of a kind takes the divine name.
senses.whyCN: 掌控之权转为超越之能，同类之最便承袭神圣之名。

intro.en: God's deep history is uncertain, but its Germanic path is solid.
intro.cn: god 的更早来源不确定，但其日耳曼语脉络可靠。

items.en: The deepest source is uncertain; no sure cognate outside Germanic is known.
items.cn: 更深的来源不确定，日耳曼语之外没有确证的同源词。

items.en: The Germanic root gudom meant the invoked or worshied one.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根 gudom 意为受呼唤、受敬拜者。

items.en: Old English god meant the deity or an image of one; neuter in the plural godu.
items.cn: 古英语 god 指神或神像，复数 godu 为中性。

items.en: Norse guð with Gothic guth reinforced the northern family.
items.cn: 诺斯语 guð 与哥特语 guth 巩固了北方词族。

items.en: Middle English capitalized God for the Christian single deity.
items.cn: 中古英语把基督教唯一神大写作 God。

items.en: Modern English kept both the many gods and the one God, and added the worship sense for people.
items.cn: 现代英语保留多神与一神两用，并引申出「被崇拜的人」。

senses.title: The precious yellow metal
senses.definition: a soft precious yellow metal used for coins, jewellery and decoration
senses.definitionCN: 用于铸币、首饰与装饰的柔软贵重黄色金属
senses.example: The ring was made of pure gold from a famous workshop.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚戒指由名坊的纯金制成。
senses.why: The core image is the heavy yellow metal that never rusts, the plain material sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是永不生锈的沉重黄色金属，是最基本的材料义项。

senses.title: Gold coins or money
senses.definition: coins made of gold, or wealth in general
senses.definitionCN: 金币或泛指财富
senses.example: Pirates buried their gold on the island.
senses.exampleCN: 海盗把金币埋在岛上。
senses.why: The metal was money itself for centuries, so coins and riches keep the name.
senses.whyCN: 数百年间这种金属就是货币本身，金币与财富便沿用其名。

senses.title: The colour of gold
senses.definition: a bright yellow colour like that of the metal
senses.definitionCN: 像黄金般的明亮黄色
senses.example: The sunset turned the whole sky gold.
senses.exampleCN: 落日把整个天空染成金色。
senses.why: The metal's colour is its most visible mark, so the colour borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 金属的颜色是最醒目的标志，颜色便借用其名。

senses.title: A gold medal or first prize
senses.definition: a medal made of or gilded with gold, given to the winner
senses.definitionCN: 给优胜者的金牌或头奖
senses.example: She won gold in the swimming final.
senses.exampleCN: 她在游泳决赛中夺得金牌。
senses.why: First place is the highest prize, and gold was always the highest metal.
senses.whyCN: 冠军是最高的奖赏，而金历来是最高等的金属。

senses.title: Made of or like gold
senses.definition: made of gold, or resembling gold in value or colour
senses.definitionCN: 由金制成，或在价值或颜色上像金
senses.example: He gave her a gold bracelet on her birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 他生日那天送了她一条金手链。
senses.why: The noun turns into an adjective when the material or colour describes a thing.
senses.whyCN: 当材料或颜色修饰事物时，名词便转为形容词。

senses.title: Of the colour of gold

senses.exampleCN: 放学后孩子们跑过金色的田野。
senses.why: The colour of the metal is painted onto hair, fields and sand.

senses.title: Made of solid gold
senses.definition: made of real gold

senses.exampleCN: 她把金项链收在天鹅绒盒子里。

senses.title: Precious and excellent
senses.definition: outstandingly good and valuable, as in a golden opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 格外优秀且宝贵，如绝佳的机会
senses.example: This is a golden opportunity to learn from the master.

senses.why: Gold was always the most precious metal, so chances as precious as gold are golden.
senses.whyCN: 金历来最贵重，于是像金一样难得的机会便是 golden。

senses.title: Prosperous and flourishing

senses.example: They held a golden wedding party after fifty years together.

definition_zh: 高尔夫球（运动）；打高尔夫球
definition_en: a game in which players hit a small ball into a series of holes using clubs
core_image: 一杆挥出：小球被送向远处的球洞
scene: 周末的球场边，爸爸教儿子如何握杆。They played golf on the course by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 golf 是「高尔夫球运动」（第 1 个义项：以杆击球入洞的游戏）；句意为他们在海边的球场打高尔夫。

collocations.zh: 高尔夫球杆；高尔夫俱乐部

derivatives.zh: 由 golf 加 -er 构成，义为「打高尔夫球的人」
由 golf 加 -ing 构成，义为「打高尔夫球（活动）」
golf 与 cart 的复合词，义为「高尔夫球车」

senses.title: The game itself
senses.definition: an outdoor game of hitting a small ball into a series of holes with the fewest strokes
senses.definitionCN: 用最少的杆数把小球打进一连串球洞的户外运动
senses.example: They played golf on the course by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边的球场打高尔夫。
senses.why: The core image is one swing aimed at a far hole, so the whole game takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是朝远处球洞的一记挥杆，整项运动由此得名。

senses.title: To play the game
senses.definition: to spend time playing golf
senses.definitionCN: 以打高尔夫球度过时间
senses.example: He golfs with his clients every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 他每周五与客户打高尔夫。
senses.why: The game name becomes the action of playing it.
senses.whyCN: 运动名转为打球这一动作。

senses.title: The equipment round
senses.definition: the set of clubs and balls used in the game
senses.definitionCN: 比赛所用的一套球杆与球
senses.example: He bought a new set of golf for the season.
senses.exampleCN: 他为这个赛季购置了一套新球具。
senses.why: The game stands for its tools, so a full set is called a golf.
senses.whyCN: 运动转指其装备，整套器具也被称为 golf。

senses.title: A golf social circle
senses.definition: the social world built around playing golf
senses.definitionCN: 围绕这项运动的社交圈
senses.example: Many business deals are made over golf.
senses.exampleCN: 许多生意在打高尔夫时谈成。
senses.why: Business people meet on the course, so the game also names the circle.
senses.whyCN: 生意人在球场相聚，这项运动也指代那个圈子。

senses.title: A leisure lifestyle
senses.definition: a relaxed lifestyle marked by playing golf
senses.definitionCN: 以打球为标志的悠闲生活方式
senses.example: After retirement they live a golf and garden life.
senses.exampleCN: 退休后他们过着高尔夫与花园式的生活。
senses.why: Free afternoons on the green become a way of life, so the word reaches the lifestyle.
senses.whyCN: 绿茵上的闲暇下午沉淀为生活方式，词义随之延伸。

intro.en: Golf's Dutch origin theory is old but not fully settled; the Scottish record is firm.
intro.cn: 高尔夫源于荷兰的说法流传已久但未完全定论；苏格兰的记录确凿。

items.en: Some link golf to Dutch kolf, a stick game; the link is debated.
items.cn: 一说与荷兰语 kolf（棍戏）有关，此说仍有争议。

items.en: The first Scottish records spell it gouf in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 最早的苏格兰记录在十五世纪拼作 gouf。

items.en: Scottish law of 1457 banned golf so men would practise archery.
items.cn: 一四五七年的苏格兰法令禁打高尔夫，让男子专心练箭。

items.en: Another theory links golf to Scots gowf, meaning a blow or strike; it is also unproven.
items.cn: 另一说把 golf 与苏格兰语 gowf（一击）相连，同样未获确证。

items.en: Modern English standardized the spelling golf and spread the game worldwide.
items.cn: 现代英语统一拼写为 golf，并把运动推向世界。

note.en: The words below resemble golf in sound or share the sport field.
note.cn: 以下词与 golf 音近，或同属运动义场。

entries.definition: One who plays golf.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「高尔夫球员」，由 golf 直接派生。

entries.definition: A large bay of the sea; vowel differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「海湾；鸿沟」，与 golf 元音不同，词源不同。

entries.definition: A wild animal; rhymes with golf.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「狼」，与 golf 押韵，词义无关。

entries.definition: A racket sport played on a court.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「网球」，另一种流行球类运动。

entries.definition: A bat-and-ball team sport.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「板球」，同为击球入靶类运动。

entries.definition: A lawn game of rolling balls to a target.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「草地滚球」，同为滚向目标的运动。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of golf.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: The Dutch kolf theory links golf to a medieval stick game.
normal.cn: 荷兰语 kolf 理论把 golf 与中世纪棍戏相联系。

normal.en: Scotland banned golf in 1457 to protect archery practice.
normal.cn: 苏格兰一四五七年禁高尔夫以保射箭训练。

normal.en: Golf course means the field where the game is played.
normal.cn: golf course 指打球的场地。

normal.en: Golfer adds the doer ending -er to golf.
normal.cn: golfer 给 golf 加上施动者后缀 -er。

normal.en: Many business talks happen during a round of golf.
normal.cn: 许多商务洽谈在打一轮高尔夫时进行。

abstract.en: Picture a small white ball flying over bright green grass.
abstract.cn: 想象小白球飞过翠绿草坪。

abstract.en: See a club swinging in a smooth silver arc.
abstract.cn: 想象球杆划出流畅的银色弧线。

abstract.en: Think of a flag waving at the little hole far ahead.
abstract.cn: 想象远处小洞边的旗子随风摆动。

examples.en: They played golf on the course by the sea.
examples.cn: 他们在海边的球场打高尔夫。

examples.en: He golfs with his clients every Friday.
examples.cn: 他每周五与客户打高尔夫。

examples.en: Many business deals are made over golf.
examples.cn: 许多生意在打高尔夫时谈成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「高尔夫」——中文译名直接借其音：高高的球飞向远方的果岭；golf 四个字母对应四个词根的旧说只是趣味联想

sensesIntro.en: Golf names the game, the act of playing, the gear, the social circle and the relaxed lifestyle.
sensesIntro.cn: golf 指运动本身、打球动作、装备、社交圈与休闲生活方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one swing sending a ball toward a far hole
core.cn: 核心意象：一记挥杆把球送向远处的球洞

intro.cn: golf 是简短的基础词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no golf word; the Latin table here stays empty by rule.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中没有高尔夫相关词，按规则此处留空。
