items.exampleCN: 早期苏格兰记录拼作 gouf。

definition_zh: 好的；优质的；擅长的；善良的；好处（作名词）
definition_en: of high quality, skilled, kind, or the benefit that something brings
core_image: 达标的果子：让人放心接受的那一份
scene: 篮子里挑出最红的那只苹果递给了妹妹。She is good at drawing animals with pencils.
sceneCN: 这里 good 是「擅长的」（第 3 个义项：在某方面能力强）；句意为她擅长用铅笔画动物。

pos.zh: 好的；优质的；擅长的；善良的

derivatives.zh: 由 good 加 -ness 构成，义为「善良；美德」
由 good 加 -ly 构成，义为「相当大的；漂亮的」
good 与 will 的复合词，义为「善意；商誉」

senses.title: Of high quality
senses.definition: of a high standard or quality
senses.definitionCN: 水准或质量高的
senses.example: This knife has a good sharp edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这把刀的刃锋利好用。
senses.why: The core image is something that passes the test, the plain quality sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是通过检验的东西，即最基本的质量义。

senses.title: Kind and morally right
senses.definition: kind, honest and morally right
senses.definitionCN: 友善、诚实且合乎道德
senses.example: A good neighbour helped us move the sofa.
senses.exampleCN: 好心的邻居帮我们搬了沙发。
senses.why: What passes the moral test is good, just as what passes the quality test is good.
senses.whyCN: 通过道德检验的便是善，正如通过质量检验的便是好。

senses.title: Skilful at something
senses.definition: able to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 能把某事做好
senses.example: She is good at drawing animals with pencils.
senses.exampleCN: 她擅长用铅笔画动物。
senses.why: A hand that produces good results is called good itself.
senses.whyCN: 产出好结果的手，本身也被称为 good。

senses.title: Pleasant or enjoyable
senses.definition: pleasant, enjoyable or suitable
senses.definitionCN: 令人愉快或合适的
senses.example: We had a good time at the lakeside picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在湖边野餐玩得很开心。
senses.why: What pleases the user is good, so times and weather earn the word.
senses.whyCN: 让人称心的便是好，时光与天气也配得上这个词。

senses.title: Benefit or wellbeing
senses.definition: the advantage or benefit that something brings
senses.definitionCN: 某物带来的益处
senses.example: Regular exercise does good to the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 规律锻炼对心脏有好处。
senses.why: Goodness can be handed over, so the quality becomes a noun of benefit.
senses.whyCN: 善与好可以传递，性质便转为利益的名词。

intro.en: Good and gather may share one root: what is brought together is kept as good.
intro.cn: good 与 gather 或许同根：被聚拢保全的东西便是好的。

items.en: The deepest root is uncertain; some connect good to Germanic gather roots.
items.cn: 更深的词根不确定，一说与日耳曼「聚拢」词根相关。

items.en: Old English gōd meant good in quality, kind and valid.
items.cn: 古英语 gōd 兼指优质、善良与有效。

items.en: Norse góðr is a close relative in the same family.
items.cn: 诺斯语 góðr 是同族近亲。

items.en: Middle English set the irregular pair better and best in place.
items.cn: 中古英语固定了不规则变形 better 与 best。

items.en: Modern English expanded good into morals, skill, pleasure and benefit.
items.cn: 现代英语把 good 扩展到道德、技能、愉悦与利益。

note.en: The words below resemble good in sound or share its positive field.
note.cn: 以下词与 good 音近，或同属正面义场。

entries.definition: A deity; one letter differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神」，与 good 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: Things for sale or possessions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商品；物品」，good 的复数转义。

entries.definition: The state of being good.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「善良」，由 good 直接派生。

entries.definition: Of high quality or in good condition.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好的；健康的」。

entries.definition: Extremely good.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「极好的」，程度更强。

entries.definition: Friendly and caring toward others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「友善的」，对应善良义。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of good.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Better and best are irregular, replacing good's own endings.
normal.cn: better 与 best 是不规则变形，替换了 good 的本族词尾。

normal.en: German gut and Dutch goed are twin forms of good.
normal.cn: 德语 gut 与荷兰语 goed 是 good 的双生形式。

normal.en: Goods means merchandise, a plural noun turned from the adjective.
normal.cn: goods 指商品，由形容词转来的复数名词。

normal.en: For your own good means for your benefit.
normal.cn: for your own good 指为了你好。

normal.en: Goodness combines quality and kindness in one noun.
normal.cn: goodness 一词兼指优质与善良。

abstract.en: Picture the shiniest apple picked out of the basket.
abstract.cn: 想象从篮子里挑出的最亮的苹果。

abstract.en: See a neighbour lifting one end of your heavy sofa.
abstract.cn: 想象邻居帮你抬起沉重的沙发一头。

abstract.en: Think of a pencil sketch of a horse that looks alive.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画得活灵活现的铅笔马。

examples.en: She is good at drawing animals with pencils.
examples.cn: 她擅长用铅笔画动物。

examples.en: A good neighbour helped us move the sofa.
examples.cn: 好心的邻居帮我们搬了沙发。

examples.en: Regular exercise does good to the heart.
examples.cn: 规律锻炼对心脏有好处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「古德」——又古老又好德的品质便是「好」；good 与 god 只差一个字母

root: good 深层词根不确定，一说与日耳曼「聚拢」词根有关；古英语 gōd，比较级 better、最高级 best 借自另一个词形系统。

sensesIntro.en: Good runs from quality to kindness, skill, pleasure and the benefit things bring.
sensesIntro.cn: good 从质量延伸到善良、擅长、愉悦与利益。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the item that passes the test and is accepted
core.cn: 核心意象：通过检验、可放心接受的那一份

intro.en: Good is a Germanic base adjective; the items below are its endings and compounds.
intro.cn: good 是日耳曼基础形容词，下面列出它的词尾与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bonus means good; it is the Latin parallel, not the source of good.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bonus 意为好的，是平行的拉丁词，并非 good 的来源。

items.example: Old English gōd covered quality and morals.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 gōd 兼指质量与道德。

definition_zh: 政府；政体；治理行为；（英式）内阁、当权者；一届政府
definition_en: the group of people and institutions that direct a state, or the system by which a state is directed
core_image: 一栋办公楼里，部长们在长桌前签署文件，门外是等待答复的市民与记者
scene: 选票清点完毕的第二天，各部门才把拖欠已久的数字挂到网站上。The government published the figures only after the votes were counted.
sceneCN: 这里 government 指掌握行政权的政府机关（第 1 个义项：作为机构整体）；句意为政府直到计票结束之后才公布那些数字。

pos.zh: 政府；政体（可数，指一届政府或一种政体；不可数，指治理这件事）

derivatives.zh: 政府的（government + -al「……的」，由机关转指其属性）
统治；治理（拉丁 gubernare「掌舵」，由动作本身指操持事务）
治理（govern + -ance「活动」，由机关转指过程）
反政府的（anti-「反对」+ government，由机关转指对立立场）

senses.title: The governing institutions
senses.definition: the body of institutions that direct public affairs and hold executive authority
senses.definitionCN: 主导公共事务并持有行政权威的整套机构
senses.example: The government employs a third of the town's adults.
senses.exampleCN: 政府雇用了镇上三分之一的成年人。
senses.why: -ment first named the result of governing, and the result came to mean the body that does it.
senses.whyCN: -ment 先指治理的结果，结果义再转指做出这个结果的机关。

senses.title: The form of rule
senses.definition: the system by which a state is organized, such as a monarchy or a republic
senses.definitionCN: 组织国家的制度，如君主制或共和制
senses.example: They compared two forms of government across the same century.
senses.exampleCN: 他们比较了同一世纪里的两种政体。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the older meaning of direction as a system rather than a set of persons.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了较早的意思：治理是一套制度，而非一群人。

senses.title: The act of governing
senses.definition: the activity of directing a state, as distinct from the bodies that carry it out
senses.definitionCN: 主导国家的活动，区别于执行它的机构
senses.example: Good government is measured in decades, not in news cycles.
senses.exampleCN: 治理的好坏以十年计，不以新闻周期计。
senses.why: English kept the action reading alongside the institutional one, so the word can name a practice.
senses.whyCN: 英语把行为义与机构义并存下来，因此这个词也能指一种实践。

senses.title: The ministers in office
senses.definition: in parliamentary usage, the prime minister and the ministers currently in office
senses.definitionCN: 在议会制用法中，指在任的首相与各部部长
senses.example: The government lost the motion by four votes.
senses.exampleCN: 内阁以四票之差输掉了动议。
senses.why: in a parliamentary system the executive sits inside the legislature, so the word narrowed to the ministers.
senses.whyCN: 在议会制中行政权坐于立法机关之内，于是这个词收窄为各部部长。

senses.title: One administration
senses.definition: a particular team holding office between one election and the next
senses.definitionCN: 在一次选举与下一次选举之间任职的特定班底
senses.example: Three governments fell within two years.
senses.exampleCN: 两年内倒掉了三届政府。
senses.why: counting administrations requires a countable noun, and this sense supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 要数「届」，就需要一个可数名词，这个义项正好提供。

senses.title: State intervention
senses.titleCN: 政府对经济与社会的干预
senses.definition: the scope of the state's active role in the economy and in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 国家在经济与日常生活中主动介入的范围
senses.example: Arguments about big government are arguments about that scope.
senses.exampleCN: 关于大政府的争论，就是关于这个范围的争论。
senses.why: the word can stand for the state's reach, which is what political argument actually disputes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以代表国家触及的范围，而政治争论争的正是这个范围。

senses.title: Self-command
senses.definition: the old sense of holding one's own conduct under control
senses.definitionCN: 把自身行为置于控制之下的旧义
senses.example: The old manuals praised government of the passions.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手册称赞对激情的自制。
senses.why: the helm image once pointed inward too, and the dictionaries record this sense from the sixteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 舵的意象也曾指向内部，词典自 16 世纪起收录此义。

senses.title: Issued by official authority
senses.titleCN: 作为修饰语：官方的、政府签发的
senses.definition: used before a noun for something issued or owned by the state
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，指由国家签发或持有的
senses.example: Government buildings line the avenue.
senses.exampleCN: 大道两旁都是政府建筑。
senses.why: attributive use lets the noun mark the source of a thing, a very common English pattern.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法让这个名词标示某物的来源，是英语中极常见的模式。

intro.en: Government is govern plus the Latin-derived suffix -ment, modelled on French gouvernement. The suffix first meant the result or means of an action, then the body that performs it. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: government 是 govern 加拉丁系后缀 -ment，仿法语 gouvernement 构成。该后缀先指动作的结果或手段，再指执行动作的机关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gubernare 'to steer a ship' supplied the verb, and its metaphorical sense of directing people was already Latin.
items.cn: gubernare「操船」提供了动词，其「引导人」的隐喻义在拉丁语中已有。

items.en: Old French gouvernement meant 'administration, direction' in the fourteenth century, with the stress on the activity.
items.cn: 古法语 gouvernement 在 14 世纪指「管理、指引」，重心在活动本身。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century as the act of governing, keeping the abstract sense alive beside the concrete one.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入，指治理这一行为，使抽象义与具体义并存。

items.en: By the sixteenth century government commonly named the persons and bodies that rule, a shift from doing to the doers.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，government 常指统治的人与机关，重心从「做」转到「做的人」。

items.en: In parliamentary usage the word narrowed further to the ministers in office, while American usage kept it for the whole executive branch.
items.cn: 在议会制用法中，这个词进一步收窄为在任部长；美式用法则保留指整个行政部门。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation for the institutional sense is not precisely dated, and the pre-Greek origin of the steering verb behind gubernare is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：机构义的最早英语书证没有确切年代；gubernare 背后那个操船动词在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one shares the govern stem; group two holds words for the state and for rule.
note.cn: 第一组共享 govern 词干；第二组是关于国家与统治的词。

entries.definition: The practice and quality of directing, including accountability; government names the body that holds authority.
entries.definitionCN: 引导的实践与品质，含问责；government 指持有权威的机关。

entries.definition: To direct or rule; the noun adds the institutional result of that activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指引或统治；名词加上这一活动所形成的机构结果。

entries.definition: A single official heading a state or institution; it names one seat, not the whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 领导一州或一机构的单个官员；指一个席位，而非整体。

entries.definition: Of a governor, from Latin gubernator; the form looks foreign but belongs to the same helm family.
entries.definitionCN: 指州长的，来自拉丁 gubernator；词形看着陌生，却属同一个舵的词族。

entries.definition: The political entity as a whole, including territory and people; government is only its directing apparatus.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的政治实体，含领土与人民；government 只是它的主导机关。

entries.definition: In American usage a president's team in office; elsewhere it means management, so it is narrower than government.
entries.definitionCN: 美式用法指总统的执政班底；其他地方指管理，因此比 government 更窄。

entries.definition: A system of rule, often with a hint of harshness or of recent imposition; government is the plainer word.
entries.definitionCN: 一套统治秩序，常暗含严苛或新近强加之意；government 是更中性的说法。

entries.definition: The legal or accepted power to act; government is the body that normally holds such power.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的法律或公认权力；government 通常就是持有此种权力的机关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: govern + -ment: first the result of steering, then the body that steers.
normal.cn: govern + -ment：先是操舵的结果，再是操舵的机关。

normal.en: The family runs govern, government, governor, governance, governmental.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 govern、government、governor、governance、governmental。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: form a government, coalition government, local government.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：组阁、联合政府、地方政府。

normal.en: Countable and uncountable split matters: three governments fell, but government is necessary.
normal.cn: 可数与否的分野很关键：倒了三届政府，但治理本身是必要的。

normal.en: British news says the government lost the vote; American news says the administration did.
normal.cn: 英媒说内阁输掉表决，美媒说执政班底输掉表决。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where the same five people sign for a whole country.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，同样五个人替整个国家签字。

abstract.en: Picture a building that changes tenants but keeps the same letterhead.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋楼换了租客，信笺抬头却始终不变。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a tiller that must answer to a queue outside the door.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着舵，还得向门外的队列交代。

examples.en: The government raised the levy without warning the growers.
examples.cn: 政府加征费用，却没有事先通知种植者。

examples.en: Coalition governments tend to postpone unpopular decisions.
examples.cn: 联合政府往往把不得人心的决定往后拖。

examples.en: Local government carries most of the cost of the repairs.
examples.cn: 地方政府承担了修缮的大部分费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: govern（掌舵）+ ment（机构）＝ 替国家扶舵的那套班子；记「换班子不换舵」。

root: govern + -ment：govern 经古法语 governer 上溯拉丁 gubernare「操船、治理」，再上溯希腊 kybernan「掌舵」，后者更早来源不确定；-ment 源自拉丁 -mentum「结果、手段」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one helm through time: the act of steering, the system of steering, the body that steers, the ministers inside that body, one team in office, the state's reach, steering oneself, and the attributive mark of official origin.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一具舵柄穿过时间：操舵的行为、操舵的制度、操舵的机关、机关里的部长、一届执政班底、国家触及的范围、对自己操舵，以及标示官方来源的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a national tiller, inside a building that outsiders stand outside of.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶着国家的舵，人在一栋楼里，外人站在楼外。

branches.en: DOING AND DOERS: the practice and the body are the same word seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 做与做的人：实践与机关是同一个词的两面。

branches.en: THE RULEBOOK: the form of rule outlives every team that works it.
branches.cn: 规则书：政体比任何操作它的班底都活得久。

branches.en: INSIDE THE BUILDING: the ministers, then the particular team counting as one unit.
branches.cn: 楼内：先是部长们，再是被算作一个单位的特定班底。

branches.en: REACH: how far the state's hand extends into the economy.
branches.cn: 触及范围：国家这只手伸进经济多深。

branches.en: INWARD AND ADJECTIVAL: steering oneself, and marking a thing as officially issued.
branches.cn: 向内与定语：对自己操舵，以及标示某物由官方签发。

intro.en: Government is one Latin verb plus one Latin suffix, and both parts build a large English family.
intro.cn: government 是一个拉丁动词加一个拉丁后缀，两部分都构成不小的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Gubernare yields govern, governor and gubernatorial; -mentum yields government, argument and monument.
latinIntro.cn: gubernare 衍生 govern、governor、gubernatorial；-mentum 衍生 government、argument、monument。

items.example: The verb pictures a hand on the helm.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词画出扶舵的手。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.example: Government began as the result of governing.

items.exampleCN: 部长们凭借来的权威治理。

items.meaning: the body that directs a state
items.example: The government fell after the budget vote.

items.exampleCN: 多个政府机构共用这处场地。
治理比一届届政府更长久。

items.example: The governor called out the guard.
items.exampleCN: 州长调出了国民警卫队。

definition_zh: 等级；年级；成绩；评分；给……评级
definition_en: a level of quality, a school year, a mark for work, or to sort things by rank
core_image: 一级一级的台阶：按高低把东西排开
scene: 期末考试结束，老师在成绩单上写下每个学生的分数。The teacher graded every essay before the holiday.
sceneCN: 这里 grade 是「评分；打分」（第 4 个义项：给作业评定等级）；句意为老师在假期前给每篇作文打了分。

derivatives.zh: 由 grade 加 -er 构成，义为「评分者；分选机」
由 grade 加 -ing 构成，义为「评级；分级」
up 与 grade 的复合词，义为「升级」

senses.title: A level of quality or rank
senses.definition: a level of quality, size or rank in a scale
senses.definitionCN: 质量、大小或级别序列中的一档
senses.example: The fruit is sold in three grades in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这种水果在市场按三个等级出售。
senses.why: The core image is one step on a ladder of quality, so the plain sense is a rank.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是质量阶梯上的一级，最基本的义项就是等级。

senses.title: A school year
senses.definition: one year in an American school course
senses.definitionCN: 美国学制中的一学年
senses.example: My cousin is in the sixth grade this year.
senses.exampleCN: 我表弟今年上六年级。
senses.why: Learning is climbed step by step, so each year becomes one grade.
senses.whyCN: 学习逐级攀登，每一年就是一级。

senses.title: A mark for schoolwork
senses.definition: a mark or score given for a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 给作业或考试打的分数
senses.example: She got the highest grade in the spelling test.
senses.exampleCN: 她在拼写测验中得了最高分。
senses.why: The rank given to the work becomes the number on the paper.
senses.whyCN: 给作业定下的等级变成纸上的分数。

senses.title: To sort or mark by rank
senses.definition: to give a grade to something, or to sort things by quality
senses.definitionCN: 给某物定级，或按质量分类
senses.example: The teacher graded every essay before the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在假期前给每篇作文打了分。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action of placing things on the ladder.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为把物件放上阶梯的动作。

senses.title: A slope of a road
senses.definition: the degree of slope of a road or railway
senses.definitionCN: 道路或铁路的倾斜程度
senses.example: The truck slowed on the steep grade of the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在山路陡坡上放慢了速度。
senses.why: A ladder can lean: the steps become a slope measured in degrees.
senses.whyCN: 阶梯可以倾斜：一级级变成用度数衡量的坡。

intro.en: Grade comes from the Latin word for a step, and gradus is its twin.
intro.cn: grade 来自拉丁语「台阶」一词，gradus 是它的孪生形式。

items.en: Latin gradus meant a step, and gradi meant to walk in steps.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gradus 意为台阶，gradi 意为迈步。

items.en: Medieval Latin gradus named ranks and degrees in learning and the church.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 gradus 指学界与教会的品级。

items.en: French grade carried the step-and-rank sense into Romance speech.
items.cn: 法语 grade 把台阶与等级义带入罗曼语。

items.en: Middle English borrowed grade for ranks and degrees of quality.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 grade，指级别与质量度。

items.en: Modern English added the school year, the mark, the slope and the verb.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了年级、分数、坡度与动词用法。

note.cn: 以下词与 grade 音近，或同属台阶与等级义场。

entries.definition: One who grades, or a grading machine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「评分者；分选机」，由 grade 直接派生。

entries.definition: To push someone into action; sounds close.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驱使」，读音与 grade 接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Elegance or divine kindness; one letter differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「优雅；恩典」，与 grade 仅差一个字母，词源不同。

entries.definition: A position in a hierarchy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「级别；地位」，对应等级义。

entries.definition: A score given for school work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「分数」，英式常用说法。

entries.definition: One movement on a stair or in a process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「台阶；步骤」，与 grade 的「台阶」本义相近。

abstract.en: See a red pen writing numbers beside each essay.
abstract.cn: 想象红笔在每篇作文旁写下分数。

abstract.en: Think of a truck crawling up a steep mountain slope.
abstract.cn: 想象卡车缓缓爬上陡峭的山坡。

examples.cn: 老师在假期前给每篇作文打了分。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gradus 是直接祖先，台阶词族就是 grade 本族。

definition_zh: 逐渐地；逐步地；缓慢地；不知不觉地
definition_en: in small steps over a period of time, rather than suddenly or all at once
core_image: 一条折线每走一小格才抬高一丝，从不直冲向上
scene: 雨停之后，浑浊的水面一点一点变清，泥沙缓缓沉到了底下。The water gradually cleared as the sediment settled to the bottom.
sceneCN: 这里 gradually 是「逐渐地」（第 1 个义项：随时间分小步变化）；句意：随着泥沙沉到水底，水逐渐变清了。图中可辨识物件：沉降的泥沙、由浑到清的水柱、时间轴、取样瓶、缓慢下降的箭头。

pos.zh: 逐渐地；逐步地；缓慢地；不知不觉地（修饰动词、形容词或整句，位置较灵活）

derivatives.zh: 逐渐的；平缓的
渐进性
等级；坡度（同出 gradus）
梯度；坡度
毕业；毕业生

senses.title: Little by little
senses.titleCN: 逐渐地：一点一点地发生
senses.definition: in small amounts over time, so that the change is felt only after a while
senses.definitionCN: 随时间以小量发生，要过一段时间才被察觉
senses.example: The cough gradually disappeared over three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 咳嗽在三周内逐渐消失了。
senses.why: gradually is the adverb of gradual, from Latin gradus 'step'; each moment adds one small step.
senses.whyCN: gradually 是 gradual 的副词，出自拉丁 gradus“步”；每一刻只加一小步。

senses.title: Stage by stage
senses.titleCN: 逐步地：按阶段依次推进
senses.definition: stage by stage, following a planned sequence
senses.definitionCN: 按计划好的次序逐阶段进行
senses.example: The old equipment was gradually replaced over four years.
senses.exampleCN: 旧设备在四年间被逐步更换。
senses.why: The adverb can mark deliberate phasing as well as natural drift; the staircase is the same, only the builder differs.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词既可标记自然漂移，也可标记有意分批；阶梯相同，只是建造者不同。

senses.title: Without being noticed
senses.titleCN: 不知不觉地：变化小到没人留意
senses.definition: so slowly that those involved do not notice the change as it happens
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢到当事者在变化发生时都未察觉
senses.example: The town gradually lost its young people without anyone planning it.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇在无人规划的情况下不知不觉失去了年轻人。
senses.why: Small steps fall below attention; the adverb often carries this 'we only saw it afterwards' flavour.
senses.whyCN: 小步小到落在注意力之下；这个副词常带“事后才发现”的意味。

senses.title: At a slow rate
senses.definition: at a low speed, with intervals between the changes
senses.definitionCN: 以很低的速度，变化之间有明显间隔
senses.example: The glacier moves gradually, a few centimetres a day.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川缓慢移动，一天只有几厘米。
senses.why: Gradual change need not be deliberate; the adverb also simply reports a low rate of movement.
senses.whyCN: 渐进变化未必是有意的；这个副词也可以只报告很低的运动速率。

senses.title: By measured reform
senses.titleCN: 渐进式地：改革上一小步一小步走
senses.definition: by measured, incremental reform rather than by a single decisive change
senses.definitionCN: 以有节制、增量的改革方式，而非一次决定性变革
senses.example: The rules were gradually relaxed rather than abolished.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规定是被逐步放宽的，而不是被废除的。
senses.why: Policy adverbs signal pace; gradually here contrasts with overnight repeal.
senses.whyCN: 政策类副词标示节奏；此处的 gradually 与“一夜废除”相对。

senses.title: Accumulating in effect
senses.titleCN: 一点点累积地：效果叠加起来
senses.definition: in a way whose effects add up until they become large
senses.definitionCN: 以下述方式：效果不断叠加，直到变得显著
senses.example: Years of sediment gradually raised the river bed.
senses.exampleCN: 多年泥沙一点点抬高了河床。
senses.why: Many tiny increments can total a great change, which is why gradual processes surprise people with their final scale.
senses.whyCN: 许多微小增量可以累成巨大变化，这正是渐进过程常以其最终规模令人吃惊的原因。

senses.title: Easing off in slope
senses.titleCN: 平缓地：坡度一点点变化
senses.definition: of terrain or a curve, changing height with a gentle gradient
senses.definitionCN: 指地形或曲线以平缓的梯度改变高度
senses.example: The ridge gradually falls away towards the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊朝大海方向平缓地降下去。
senses.why: The same staircase image applies to ground: each metre drops only a little.
senses.whyCN: 同一阶梯意象也适用于地面：每走一米只下降一点点。

senses.title: Turning into something else
senses.titleCN: 渐渐转为：状态慢慢过渡
senses.definition: used before verbs of becoming to show a slow transition from one state to another
senses.definitionCN: 用于“变得”类动词前，表示从一种状态缓慢过渡到另一种
senses.example: The debate gradually became a quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论渐渐变成了一场争吵。
senses.why: Transitions are where gradual is most useful: the adverb marks that no single moment separates the two states.
senses.whyCN: 过渡正是 gradual 最有用之处：这个副词标记没有任何单一时刻把两种状态分开。

intro.en: Gradually is the English adjective gradual plus the adverb ending -ly, from Old English -līce. The root is Latin gradus 'step'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gradually 是英语形容词 gradual 加副词词尾 -ly（源自古英语 -līce）。词根为拉丁 gradus“步”。年代为约数。

items.en: gradus 'step, rank' came from gradi 'to walk'. The family reached English through French and directly from Latin at different periods.
items.cn: gradus“步、等级”出自 gradi“行走”。这一词族在不同时期经法语以及直接从拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: gradual is recorded in the 15th century with the sense 'step by step'. Its -al ending marks a Latin-derived adjective.
items.cn: gradual 于 15 世纪有记录，意为“一步一步地”。其 -al 词尾标记拉丁来源形容词。

items.en: -ly goes back to Old English -līce, originally a separate word meaning 'body, form'. It became the standard adverb ending and attached to Latin-derived adjectives without difficulty.
items.cn: -ly 可追溯到古英语 -līce，原为意为“身体、形态”的独立词，后成为标准副词词尾，并毫无困难地附着在拉丁来源形容词上。

items.en: Gradually became the usual adverb of slow change in ordinary prose, while the adjective remained more formal and often attributive.
items.cn: gradually 成为普通书面语中表示缓慢变化的常用副词，而形容词 gradual 更正式，且多作定语。

items.en: The exact first record of gradually is uncertain, and the deeper Indo-European root behind gradi is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: gradually 的确切首见记录存疑；gradi 背后的更深印欧词根属重构，并无实际记录。

note.en: The first group contains words easily mistaken for this adverb; the second contains adverbs of slow or staged change.
note.cn: 第一组是易被误认作本副词的词；第二组是表示缓慢或分阶段变化的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective. Use it after a linking verb or before a noun; use gradually to modify an action verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词；跟在系动词后或置于名词前；修饰动作动词时应使用 gradually。

entries.definition: Not an English word; it is a common misspelling produced by blending gradual and gradually.
entries.definitionCN: 并非英语词，是把 gradual 与 gradually 混写而成的常见错拼。

entries.definition: Continuous and not changing suddenly, as in a steady increase.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稳定的；持续的」，如稳定增长，与 gradually 的渐进义相关。

entries.definition: From grave 'serious', meaning 'seriously'. It sounds close but comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 grave“严重的”，意为“严重地”；读音接近，但来源是另一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: At a low speed; it says nothing about small steps or stages.
entries.definitionCN: 以低速度；不涉及小步或阶段。

entries.definition: Stage by stage and usually with a direction of advance; often slightly approving.

normal.cn: gradual + -ly：“一步一步”的副词形式。

examples.en: Scientists gradually came to accept that the climate had shifted.
examples.cn: 科学家们渐渐接受了气候已经改变这一事实。

examples.en: The path climbs gradually for the first kilometre, then turns steep.

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses are one adverb doing one job: marking change that arrives in small steps, whether in time, in policy, in slope or in a state of mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一个副词在做一件事：标记以小步到来的变化，无论这变化在时间、政策、坡度还是心境上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that rises by tiny increments and never jumps.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条以小增量上升、从不跳跃的线。

branches.en: ACCUMULATION: tiny steps add up, and the adverb covers both the adding and the final size.
branches.cn: 累积：微小步子叠加起来，这个副词既覆盖叠加过程，也覆盖最终规模。

branches.en: DESIGNED PACE: staged replacement and stepwise reform give the staircase a planner.
branches.cn: 设计节奏：分批更换与逐步改革为这条阶梯安排了设计者。

branches.en: BELOW ATTENTION: steps small enough to escape notice are the adverb's most characteristic effect.
branches.cn: 低于注意力：小到不被察觉的步子，是这个副词最典型的效应。

branches.en: RATE AND GROUND: low speed and gentle gradient are the same measure applied to motion and terrain.
branches.cn: 速率与地面：低速与缓坡是同一尺度分别用于运动与地形。

branches.en: TRANSITION: before verbs of becoming, the adverb marks a slow crossing between two states.
branches.cn: 过渡：在“变得”类动词前，这个副词标记两种状态之间的缓慢跨越。

intro.en: Gradually is gradual plus -ly, the standard English adverb ending. The Latin root grad- carries the 'step' image.
intro.cn: gradually 是 gradual 加 -ly，即标准英语副词词尾。拉丁词根 grad- 承载“步”的意象。

latinIntro.en: The grad- family spreads across English verbs and nouns: grade, gradient, gradual, graduate, degrade, upgrade and retrograde.
latinIntro.cn: grad- 词族遍布英语动词与名词：grade、gradient、gradual、graduate、degrade、upgrade、retrograde。

senses.title: A person who holds a degree
senses.definition: someone who has completed a degree or a course of study
senses.definitionCN: 已完成学位或一段学业的人
senses.example: The firm hires two graduates each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司每年春天招聘两名毕业生。
senses.why: the Latin past participle graduatus named someone advanced step by step, and English kept it as the word for the finished student.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁过去分词 graduatus 指逐级晋升的人，英语把它保留为「学业已完成者」的称呼。

senses.title: To complete a degree
senses.definition: to finish a course of study and be formally awarded a degree
senses.definitionCN: 读完一段学业并被正式授予学位
senses.example: She graduated from the programme and now works in the same lab.
senses.exampleCN: 她从该项目毕业，如今在同一间实验室工作。
senses.why: the verb began as 'to take a degree' in Medieval Latin, so it names the moment of formal completion.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在中世纪拉丁语中本为「取得学位」，因此它命名的正是正式完成的那一刻。

senses.title: To move up a level
senses.definition: to move from one stage or rank to a higher one
senses.definitionCN: 从一个阶段或等级升到更高的一级
senses.example: The junior clerk graduated to head of section in four years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位低级职员四年内升到科长。
senses.why: the step image survives outside school: any promotion or transfer upward can be called a graduation.
senses.whyCN: 台阶意象在校外仍然存活：任何向上晋升或转入更高位置都可称为 graduate。

senses.title: Postgraduate, as an adjective
senses.definition: describing study or a school that comes after a first degree
senses.definitionCN: 描述取得首个学位之后的学业或院校
senses.example: He moved into graduate study after two years of teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 教了两年书之后，他转入研究生学习。
senses.why: American usage fixed the adjective to the stage above the bachelor's degree, which is why graduate school names a place, not a person.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把这个形容词固定在学士之上的阶段，因此「研究生院」这类说法指的是一个地方而非一个人。

senses.title: To mark a scale in degrees
senses.definition: to divide a vessel or instrument into regular measured marks
senses.definitionCN: 把容器或仪器分成规则的测量刻线
senses.example: The glass was graduated in millilitres on one side.
senses.exampleCN: 这只玻璃器皿一侧按毫升划了刻度。
senses.why: the oldest technical sense is physical: to graduate a vessel is to give it steps that can be read.
senses.whyCN: 最早的技术义是物理性的：给容器「分度」就是给它可读的台阶。

senses.title: A secondary-school finisher
senses.definition: in American usage, a person who has finished high school
senses.definitionCN: 在美式用法中，指读完高中的人
senses.example: Half the town turned out for the high school graduates.
senses.exampleCN: 半个镇子的人都出来为高中毕业生庆祝。
senses.why: American speech widened the noun downward to secondary school, so the word no longer guarantees a degree.
senses.whyCN: 美式口语把名词向下扩展到中学，因此这个词不再保证持有学位。

senses.title: To pass through stages
senses.definition: to change by small steps from one condition to another
senses.definitionCN: 以一种状态按小步转入另一种状态
senses.example: The colours graduate from pale yellow to deep orange.
senses.exampleCN: 色彩从浅黄逐步过渡到深橙。
senses.why: the step sense turns abstract again here: a continuous change is read as a series of degrees.
senses.whyCN: 台阶义在此再次抽象化：连续的变化被读成一串度数。

senses.title: A trained programme finisher
senses.titleCN: 完成培训项目的结业者
senses.definition: a person who has completed a specified training programme, as in nursing
senses.definitionCN: 完成某项特定培训项目的人，如护理专业
senses.example: The ward employs two nurse graduates from the new cohort.
senses.exampleCN: 该病区雇用了新一批护理专业的结业者。
senses.why: training programmes use the noun for anyone who has finished their course, whether or not a degree is awarded.
senses.whyCN: 培训项目用这个名词指任何完成课程的人，无论是否授予学位。

intro.en: Graduate comes from Latin graduatus, the past participle of graduari 'to take a degree', from gradus 'step'. The noun and the marking verb entered English by different routes in the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: graduate 来自拉丁 graduatus，即 graduari「取得学位」的过去分词，源于 gradus「台阶」。名词与「划刻度」的动词用法在十五与十七世纪经不同路径进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Gradus meant 'step, stride, degree', the shared source of the stair and the scale.
items.cn: gradus 意为「台阶、步伐、度数」，是楼梯与量具的共同来源。

items.en: Graduari meant 'to take a degree, to be advanced step by step'. It described the student who had climbed all the required steps.
items.cn: graduari 意为「取得学位、逐级晋升」，描述已爬完所有必需台阶的学生。

items.en: The past participle graduatus named the person who had been advanced, and it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 过去分词 graduatus 指已被晋升的人，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: English graduate appeared in the fifteenth century for a person holding a degree, and the university sense dominated for centuries.
items.cn: 英语 graduate 于十五世纪出现，指持有学位的人，此后数百年间以大学义为主。

items.en: In the seventeenth century the same form was used as a verb for dividing a vessel into degrees, which is why a graduated cylinder carries the word without any school.
items.cn: 十七世纪，同一词形被用作动词，指把容器分成度数，因此在「刻度量筒」这样的说法里，这个词与学校毫无关系。

items.en: The deeper origin of gradus and gradi is uncertain; the link to a root meaning 'to step, go' is a reconstruction. The American widening of the noun to secondary school is recent and only loosely documented.
items.cn: gradus 与 gradi 的更早来源不确定；与表示「迈步、行走」的词根的联系属重构形式。名词在美式用法中向中学扩展是晚近现象，记录亦不严密。

note.en: Group one holds the step-root family, including the two words most often confused with this one; group two holds the people and stages around finishing study.
note.cn: 第一组是「台阶」词根词族，包括最易与它混淆的两个词；第二组是围绕完成学业的人与阶段。

entries.definition: The act, the ceremony or the scale marks; graduate is the person or the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指行为、仪式或刻度；graduate 指人或动词。

entries.definition: Changing little by little; it describes pace, not the completion of study.
entries.definitionCN: 指一点一点变化，描述节奏而非完成学业。

entries.definition: The institution for study after a first degree; the adjective sense lives mainly in this and similar compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 指取得首个学位后就读的院校；形容词义主要活在此类复合词中。

entries.definition: A student who has not yet taken a first degree, the rung below the graduate.
entries.definitionCN: 指尚未取得首个学位的学生，是 graduate 下面的一级。

entries.definition: A former student of a particular school, whether or not recently graduated; it stresses loyalty to the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指某校的旧生，无论是否刚毕业；强调对院校的归属。

entries.definition: British usage for study after a bachelor's degree, close to the adjective sense of graduate.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指学士之后的学业，接近 graduate 的形容词义。

entries.definition: A British term for someone finishing secondary school, with no implication of a degree.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指读完中学的人，不含学位之意。

entries.definition: The holder of a first degree, a specific rank rather than a general finisher.
entries.definitionCN: 指首个学位的持有者，是具体等级而非泛称的完成者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real step root, the real double life of the word in schools and laboratories, and the real American usage.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的台阶词根、这个词在学校与实验室之间的真实双重身份，以及真实的美式用法。

normal.en: gradus 'step': a graduate has reached the top of the stair.
normal.cn: gradus「台阶」：graduate 已走到楼梯顶端。

normal.en: Graduari 'to take a degree' gave the noun; to graduate a vessel gave the measuring verb.
normal.cn: graduari「取得学位」给出名词；给容器分度则给出测量的动词义。

normal.en: The family runs graduation, gradual, gradually, undergraduate, postgraduate.
normal.cn: 词族包括 graduation、gradual、gradually、undergraduate、postgraduate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the school sense: graduate from, graduate school, graduate student.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出学校义：从……毕业、研究生院、研究生。

normal.en: The laboratory keeps the measuring sense: a graduated cylinder is read at the eye line.
normal.cn: 实验室保留测量义：量筒的读数要与视线齐平。

abstract.cn: 想象一顶帽子被抛到一片相同毕业袍的上方。

abstract.en: Picture a glass tube ruled with fine lines, standing beside a diploma on the same bench.
abstract.cn: 想象一根划着细线的玻璃管，与一张文凭并排放在同一张台上。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase that continues past the stage and out of the building.

examples.cn: 她从北方一所小学院毕业。

examples.en: The scheme hires recent graduates for two-year placements.

examples.cn: 柜中每件器皿都按毫升划了刻度。

root: 拉丁 gradus「台阶、度数」（源自 gradi「迈步」）→ graduari「取得学位」→ 过去分词 graduatus → 英语 graduate；十七世纪同一词形又用作「给量具分度」。gradus 与 gradi 的更早来源不确定，与「迈步」词根的联系属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses climb one stair and then leave the school: a person reaches the top, the reaching becomes a verb, an upward move, a postgraduate adjective, a scale on a glass vessel, a high-school finisher, a gradual change and a trained programme finisher.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先爬同一座楼梯，再走出校门：有人走到顶端，到达成为动词、向上的晋升、研究生的形容词、玻璃器皿上的刻度、中学结业者、渐变，以及完成培训项目的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a staircase that continues past the stage and out of the building, while a ruled glass tube stands on the same bench as a diploma.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座越过舞台、延伸出楼外的楼梯，而一根划着刻度的玻璃管与文凭并排放在同一张台上。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE ACT: the one at the top and the moment of arriving share one form.
branches.cn: 人与动作：站在顶端的人与到达的那一刻共用同一词形。

branches.en: THE NEXT STAGE: an upward move at work, and the adjective for study above a first degree.
branches.cn: 下一阶段：职场上的向上晋升，以及首个学位之后学业的形容词。

branches.en: THE RULED LINE: a vessel is divided into degrees, and continuous change is read as degrees too.
branches.cn: 刻线：器皿被分成度数，连续变化也被读成度数。

branches.en: THE WIDER NOUN: American speech lowers the word to secondary school, so a degree is no longer guaranteed.
branches.cn: 更宽的名词：美式口语把词降到中学，学位不再是保证。

branches.en: THE COURSE: any training programme can produce a graduate, degree or not.
branches.cn: 课程：任何培训项目都能产出结业者，有没有学位都一样。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root and participle ending, and the same pieces build the school family and the measuring words.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁词根与分词词尾构成，同一批部件造出学校词族与测量类词。

latinIntro.en: Gradus and gradi supply the step; graduari and its participle graduatus supply the person and the verb, while the same form was reused for marking a scale.
latinIntro.cn: gradus 与 gradi 提供「台阶」；graduari 及其分词 graduatus 提供人与动词，而同一词形又被用于划刻度。

senses.title: The rules of a language
senses.definition: the whole system of rules for words and sentences in a language
senses.definitionCN: 一门语言组词成句的整套规则
senses.example: The pupil learned grammar rules from the new textbook.
senses.exampleCN: 学生从新课本学习语法规则。
senses.why: The core image is a hidden manual behind every sentence, so the plain sense is the rule system.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是每个句子背后的隐形手册，最基本的义项就是规则体系。

senses.title: Correct or incorrect use
senses.definition: the degree to which someone speaks or writes correctly
senses.definitionCN: 说话或写作符合语法的程度
senses.example: Her grammar improved a lot after one term.
senses.exampleCN: 一学期后她的语法进步很大。
senses.why: The rules can be kept or broken, so the word also measures correctness.
senses.whyCN: 规则可守可破，词义便兼指正确程度。

senses.title: A book of rules
senses.definition: a book that describes the grammar of a language
senses.definitionCN: 描述一门语言语法的书
senses.example: He kept an old grammar on his desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他桌上放着一本旧语法书。
senses.why: The rules are printed and bound, so the book borrows the system's name.
senses.whyCN: 规则被印订成册，书便沿用体系之名。

senses.title: The structural system of a field
senses.definition: the basic structure of a subject or art beyond language
senses.definitionCN: 语言之外领域的基本结构
senses.example: The teacher explained the grammar of the dance steps.
senses.exampleCN: 老师讲解了舞步的结构法则。
senses.why: Any craft with fixed rules is said to have its own grammar.
senses.whyCN: 凡有固定规则的技艺都被说成有自己的 grammar。

senses.title: A grammar school tradition
senses.definition: a secondary school historically focused on Latin grammar
senses.definitionCN: 历史上以拉丁语法为核心的中等学校
senses.example: She entered a famous grammar school in town.
senses.exampleCN: 她进了镇上著名的文法学校。
senses.why: Old schools taught grammar above all, so the subject names the school.
senses.whyCN: 旧式学校以语法为纲，学科名便转指学校。

intro.en: Grammar goes back to the Greek art of letters, and glamour is its surprising cousin.
intro.cn: grammar 可追溯到希腊语的「文字之艺」，glamour 是它令人意外的亲戚。

items.en: Greek gramma meant a written letter, and grammata the letters of the alphabet.
items.cn: 希腊语 gramma 意为字母，grammata 指整套字母。

items.en: Greek grammatike techne meant the art of letters, that is, the study of language.
items.cn: 希腊语 grammatike techne 意为文字之艺，即语言之学。

items.en: Latin grammatica carried the art-of-letters sense into scholarship.
items.cn: 拉丁语 grammatica 把文字之艺带入学问传统。

items.en: Old French gramaire passed the word on with both learning and magic tinges.
items.cn: 古法语 gramaire 传词时兼带学问与魔法色彩。

items.en: Middle English borrowed it as gramere; the rival spelling glamour kept the magic shade.
items.cn: 中古英语借作 gramere；竞争拼法 glamour 保留了魔法色彩。

items.en: Modern English fixed grammar for the rules, and grammar school named the old schools.
items.cn: 现代英语定为 grammar，grammar school 指旧式学校。

note.en: The words below resemble grammar in sound or share its learning field.
note.cn: 以下词与 grammar 音近，或同属语言学习义场。

entries.definition: Following the rules of grammar.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「合乎语法的」，由 grammar 派生。

entries.definition: Enchanting charm; historically the same word as grammar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「魅力」，与 grammar 历史上同源。

entries.definition: A unit of weight; one letter differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「克」，与 grammar 拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The arrangement of words in sentences.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「句法」，语法的一部分。

entries.definition: The way words are actually used.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「惯用法」，与规则互补。

entries.definition: The system of marks in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「标点」，与语法并列的规则体系。

normalIntro.en: Five links to real forms and uses of grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实构形与用法的联想。

normal.en: Greek gramma meant letter, the seed of grammar and diagram alike.
normal.cn: 希腊语 gramma 意为字母，是 grammar 与 diagram 的种子。

normal.en: Glamour began as a Scottish variant of grammar meaning magic.
normal.cn: glamour 起初是 grammar 的苏格兰变体，意为魔法。

normal.en: Grammar school names schools that taught Latin grammar first.
normal.cn: grammar school 指以拉丁语法起家的学校。

normal.en: Grammatical adds -ical to grammar for the adjective.
normal.cn: grammatical 给 grammar 加 -ical 构成形容词。

normal.en: Bad grammar in speech marks sentences that break the rules.
normal.cn: bad grammar 指违反规则的口语句子。

abstract.en: Picture a table of sentence parts pinned to the classroom wall.
abstract.cn: 想象教室墙上钉着一张句子成分表格。

abstract.en: See arrows running from subject to verb to object.
abstract.cn: 想象箭头从主语连到动词再到宾语。

abstract.en: Think of an old book with rules written in faded ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一本旧书，规则用褪色墨水写成。

examples.en: The pupil learned grammar rules from the new textbook.
examples.cn: 学生从新课本学习语法规则。

examples.en: Her grammar improved a lot after one term.
examples.cn: 一学期后她的语法进步很大。

examples.en: He kept an old grammar on his desk.
examples.cn: 他桌上放着一本旧语法书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「格莱默」——按格子排列句子就不会默默犯错；grammar 管着每个词的位置

root: grammar 源自希腊语 gramma（字母）与 grammatike techne（文字之艺），经拉丁语 grammatica、古法语 gramaire 进入英语；glamour 为其同源变体。

sensesIntro.en: Grammar runs from the rule system to correctness, the book, other rule-bound arts and the old schools.
sensesIntro.cn: grammar 从规则体系延伸到正误、语法书、其他规则化技艺与旧式学校。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the hidden manual behind every sentence
core.cn: 核心意象：每个句子背后的隐形规则手册

intro.en: Grammar is a Greek-root base; the items below are its endings and kin words.
intro.cn: grammar 是希腊词根的基础词，下面列出它的词尾与同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin grammatica is the direct carrier, so the Latin family belongs to grammar's own line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 grammatica 是直接传递者，拉丁词族即 grammar 本族。

items.example: Greek gramma seeded the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 gramma 孕育了整个词族。
